when he killed his brother. For his hands gave birth to what his mind had conceived. But the purity of Abel’s heart was his prayer.
Now I will show you, my beloved, that fire used to lick up all the offerings that were accepted.
For when Manoah, Samson’s father, presented an offering, living fire came down and licked it up, and in that flame the angel who had spoken with him ascended to heaven.
And when God confirmed to Abraham the promise that a son would be born to him, he told him, “Take a three-year-old heifer and a three-year-old female goat,
and a turtledove and a young pigeon.” When Abraham slaughtered them, split them, and placed each piece opposite its counterpart, stillness fell upon him, and there was darkness.
Fire came down, passed between the halves, and consumed Abraham’s offering. Also the offerings that used to be presented in the Tent of Meeting,
It was living fire that came down to consume them. Likewise, when Aaron’s sons, Nadab and Abihu, treated the service of the offering with contempt,
fire came down as usual at the time of the offering, but it did not find their offerings pure and did not approach them.
When they saw that the offering had not been consumed, they brought foreign fire to consume it, so that Moses would not rebuke them, asking why the offering had not been consumed.
The foreign fire consumed the offering, but this fire from heaven consumed them themselves. The Lord’s holiness was shown through them because they had treated his service with contempt.
Likewise, when two hundred and fifty men rebelled against Moses and presented censers without being commanded, that fire was given a command
and went out from before the Lord and consumed them. Their censers were consecrated at the cost of their lives. Again, when Solomon built the temple
and presented sacrifices and burnt offerings, he prayed, and fire came down from heaven and consumed the fat of the burnt offerings on the altar. Again, when Elijah presented an offering,
fire came down and consumed it. His offering was accepted like Abel’s, while that of Baal’s worshipers was rejected like Cain’s.
I have written all this evidence about fire to you to establish for you the statement that fire consumed Abel’s offering.
Now listen, my dear friend, concerning this pure prayer and how many mighty deeds have been displayed through it. For when Abraham prayed,

he brought back the captives of the five kings. Through his prayer, too, a barren woman gave birth. And through the power of his prayer he received the promise that the nations would be blessed through his offspring.
Isaac also showed the power of prayer when he prayed for Rebekah and she gave birth, and for Abimelech, and wrath was withheld from him.
Our father Jacob also prayed at Bethel and saw the gate of heaven open, and a ladder leading up to the heights.
This is the symbol of our Savior that Jacob saw: the gate of heaven is Christ, as he said, “I am the gate of life;
whoever enters through me will live forever.” David also said, “This is the gate of the Lord, through which the righteous enter.”
The ladder that Jacob saw is also a symbol of our Savior, through whom righteous people ascend from the lower world to the upper world.
It is also a symbol of our Savior’s cross, which was raised up like a ladder. “The Lord,” it says, “stands above it.” For above Christ is the Lord of all,
as the blessed apostle said, “The head of Christ is God.” Jacob called that place Bethel.
There Jacob set up a stone pillar as a witness and poured oil on its top. Our father Jacob also did this beforehand as a symbol:
that stones would receive anointing. For the nations who have believed in Christ are the ones who are anointed, as John said about them,
“From these stones God can raise up children for Abraham.” For in Jacob’s prayer the mystery of the calling of the nations was revealed beforehand.
See, then, my dear friend, how many mysteries are hidden in the vision that Jacob saw. For he saw the gate of heaven, which is Christ,
and he saw the ladder, the symbol of the cross. He anointed the stones, a representation of the nations, and vowed to give tithes to Levi.
For hidden within him were those who give tithes and those who receive firstfruits. And in his loins was Judah, the lion’s cub,
in whom Christ the King was hidden. In him he displayed anointing, and the tribes within him made vows to the Levites.
The kings who were in his loins made his heart proud, and the spirit of the prophets who were destined to come from his offspring tested him.
With his staff alone he crossed the Jordan. He already held a wonderful mystery in his hand: the sign of the cross of the great Prophet.
He set out for the land of the people of the East, because from him light dawned upon the nations. He rested beside the well that had a stone over its mouth,
which a whole company could not lift. For many shepherds could not lift it and open the well,
until Jacob came. By the power of the Shepherd who was hidden within his loins, he lifted the stone and watered his flock. Many prophets came,
but they could not uncover the baptismal font until the great Prophet came. He alone opened it and was baptized in it, and he cried out in his gracious voice,
“Let everyone who is thirsty come to me and drink.” Jacob also prayed when he returned from Laban, and he was rescued from the hands of his brother Esau.
He prayed in this way, giving thanks and saying, “With my staff I crossed this Jordan, and now I have become two camps.”
O wonderful mystery of our Savior! For when our Lord first came, a shoot came forth from the stock of Jesse, like Jacob’s staff.
When he returned from his Father at his second coming, he went to him with two camps: one from the people and the other from the nations,
like Jacob, who returned to his father Isaac with two camps. For Jacob returned with his eleven sons,
and our Savior’s eleven disciples come with him, because Judas is not with them. Afterward Benjamin was born, and Jacob’s sons became twelve.
Afterward Tolmai was chosen, and our Savior’s disciples became twelve. This is the account of Jacob’s prayer.
But what shall we say about the limitless power of Moses’ prayer? For his prayer saved him from Pharaoh’s hands.
It showed him the dwelling place of his God. Through his prayer he brought ten plagues upon Pharaoh. His prayer also divided the sea,
sweetened the bitter water, brought down manna, brought up quail, split the rock, made water flow, and defeated Amalek.
It strengthened Joshua, threw Og and Sihon into confusion in battle, brought the wicked down to Sheol, and turned his God’s wrath away from his people.
It ground the sinful calf to powder, brought the tablets down from the mountain, and made his face shine. His prayer is more extensive to recount than Jacob’s.
Joshua son of Nun also distinguished himself before his God through his prayer. His prayer divided the Jordan, and it also overthrew the walls of Jericho,
brought trouble upon Achan, held back the sun, made the moon stand still, destroyed kings, conquered the land, and gave it as an inheritance to the Israelites.
Let us turn to the silent prayer that Hannah, Samuel’s mother, prayed. It was pleasing to God and ended her barrenness,
removed her disgrace, and brought forth a Nazirite and priest. Samuel also prayed before his God when he became a sign to the Israelites,
when he made their sins known to them because they had asked for a king. Samuel offered a burnt offering on the altar, and rain fell during the wheat harvest.
David also prayed before his God and was rescued from Saul’s hands. He also prayed when he counted the people, and wrath and anger turned away from them,
when the destroyer had power over them. Asa also prayed, and his prayer displayed great power when Zerah the Indian came out against him.
And an army of a million was with him. Then Asa prayed and said, “By this your power is made known, our God: when you deliver a great people into the hands of a small people.”
God heard his prayer and sent his angel and threw them into confusion. The great army was defeated through the power of Asa’s prayer. And Jehoshaphat his son also—
his prayer destroyed the army of his enemies and defeated them. Hezekiah also prayed, and a hundred and eighty-five thousand—
his prayer struck down through the angel, the commander of the army. Jonah also prayed before his God from the depths of the sea,
and he was heard and answered and delivered unharmed. For his prayer pierced the depths, overcame the waves, mastered the billows, pierced the cloud,
flew through the air, opened heaven, and approached the throne of majesty through Gabriel, who presents prayers before God.
The depths disgorged the prophet, and the fish cast Jonah out onto dry land. Again, Hananiah, Azariah, and Mishael—their prayer overcame the flame,
cooled the fire’s fierceness, changed its burning nature, subdued the king’s anger, and rescued the righteous men.
Daniel also prayed, and his prayer shut the mouths of the lions. Their devouring mouths were kept from the flesh and bones of the righteous man.
The lions spread out their paws and caught Daniel so that he would not fall to the ground. They embraced him in their arms,
and they kissed his feet. When Daniel stood in the pit to pray, they too stretched out their paws toward heaven, just as Daniel did.
The one who receives prayers came down to them and shut the lions’ mouths. For Daniel said to Darius, “My God sent his angel
and shut the lions’ mouths, and they did not harm me.” For the pit was covered and sealed, yet light shone within it.
Those lions rejoiced because, on account of Daniel, they had seen the light. For when Daniel grew drowsy and wanted to sleep,
the lions lowered themselves so that he could sleep on them rather than on the ground. For that pit was brighter than an upper room with many windows.
He multiplied his prayers there beyond those in his upper room, where he used to pray only three times. Daniel came up victorious,
and his accusers fell in his place. The lions’ mouths were opened, and they ate them and crushed their bones.
His prayer also brought the captives back from Babylon when seventy years were completed. And each one of our righteous fathers [?],
whenever distress came upon them, took up the weapon of prayer, and through it they were delivered from distress.
Our Savior also taught prayer and said that you should pray in secret to the Hidden One, who sees everything. For he said, “Enter your room and pray to your Father in secret,
and the Father who sees what is hidden will reward you.” But why, my dear friend, did our Savior teach and say, “Pray to your Father in secret, with the door shut”?
I will explain this to you as far as I understand it. For he said, “Pray to your Father in secret, with the door shut.” This is what it means:
Our Lord’s word shows us that he means, “Pray secretly in your heart and shut the door.” And what is the door he said to shut, if not your mouth?
For it is the temple in which Christ dwells, as the apostle said, “You are the Lord’s temple.” Let the inner person enter
this house and cleanse it of everything unclean, with the door—that is, your mouth—shut. And if this were not so,
How do you understand this matter? For if you happen to be in the wilderness, where there is no house or door, will you not pray in secret?
And if, again, you happen to be on a mountaintop, will you not pray? Our Savior showed this: that he knows the desire of the heart and mind.
As our Lord himself wrote, “Your Father knows what you need before you ask him.” And it is written in Isaiah the prophet:
“Before my chosen ones call, I will hear them; and before they cry out, I will answer them.” Again Isaiah spoke about the wicked:
“Even if you multiply your prayers, I will not listen.” Again he said, “They will cry into my ears with a loud voice, but I will not hear them.”
He said this about deceitful prayer, which is not accepted. Listen to all these words with discernment, and you will also grasp their force.
Our Life-giver said another thing there, which must be understood with discernment. For he said, “Where two or three are gathered in my name,
there I am among them.” And how will you understand this saying, my dear friend? For our Life-giver has said,
“Where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am among them.” And if you are alone, is Christ not with you?
Yet it is written about those who believe in Christ that Christ dwells in them. And did he indicate by this that only when there are two or three,
then Christ is with them? But I will show you that there are places where, instead of two or three,
more than a thousand are gathered in Christ’s name, and Christ is not with them. And there is a person who is alone, and Christ is with him.
This saying that our Life-giver spoke is fitting and beautiful for those who hear it. For he said, “Where two or three are gathered in my name,
there I am among them.” When someone gathers himself together in Christ’s name, Christ dwells in him, and God dwells in Christ.
From then on, that person becomes one of three: his own person, Christ who dwells in him, and God who is in Christ. As our Lord himself said,
“I am in my Father, and my Father is in me.” And he said, “I and my Father are one.” And again he said, “You are in me, and I am in you.”
Again he said through the prophet, “I will dwell in them and walk among them.” With this understanding you can grasp this saying that our Life-giver spoke.
And I will show you, my dear friend, that God was in each one of our righteous fathers who prayed.
For when Moses prayed on the mountain, he was alone, and God was with him. He was not left unheard because he was alone.
Rather, Moses’ prayer was heard all the more, and it calmed his God’s anger. Elijah too was alone on Mount Carmel,
and his prayer displayed wondrous powers. For through his prayer the heavens were shut, and through his prayer their bonds were again loosened.
His prayer snatched from the hands of death and delivered from Sheol. His prayer also uprooted impurity from Israel, and his prayer brought down fire
three times: once upon the altar and twice upon the captains. It brought him vengeance when the fire came down through his prayer.
He knelt on his knees and prayed, and he was answered quickly. But the four hundred and fifty who cried out with a loud voice were not heard,
because they were calling on the name of Baal. Elijah, though he was alone, was heard all the more. So too Jonah the prophet, when he prayed from the depths of Sheol,
He was heard. Though he was alone, he was quickly heard and answered. Elisha too prayed and brought someone back from Sheol.
He was rescued from the hands of the wicked who surrounded him. Although he appeared to be alone, a great army surrounded him. For he said to his disciple,
“Those with us are more numerous than those with them.” Though they were alone, they were not alone. Through this explanation I have given you,
you can understand the words of our Lord, who said, “Where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am among them.”
As I explained to you above, when you pray, direct your heart upward and your eyes downward, and enter into your inner self.
Pray in secret to your Father in heaven. All this I have written to you about prayer—that when it is pure it is heard,
and when it is not pure it is not heard—because there are people among us who multiply their prayers, prolong their pleas, and bow themselves down,
and spread out their hands, yet the deeds that belong to prayer are far from them. For they pray the prayer that our Savior taught:
“Forgive us our debts, as we too forgive our debtors.” You who pray, remember that you are presenting an offering before God.
Let the one who presents prayers not be put to shame by an offering that has a blemish. You pray to be forgiven, and you promise that you forgive.
First consider in your mind whether you forgive, and then promise, “I forgive.” Do not lie to God and say, “I forgive,”
when you do not forgive. For God is not a man like you, whom you can deceive. When one person sins against another, he can appeal to the Lord;
but when someone sins against God, to whom can he appeal? Do not condemn yourself through your prayer. Listen also to what our Lord said:
“When you present an offering and remember that you hold some resentment against your brother, leave your offering before the altar,
and go and be reconciled with your brother. Then come and present your offering.” If, while you are praying, you remember that you hold some resentment,
consider this in your mind: your prayer is left before the altar, and the one who presents prayers is unwilling to lift it from the earth.
For he examines your offering for a blemish. If it is pure, he brings it up before God. But if he finds in your prayer, “Forgive me, and I forgive,”
the one who brings prayers up says this to the person praying: “First forgive your debtor, and then I will bring your prayer up to the one to whom you owe a debt.

Forgive a hundred denarii, in keeping with your poverty, and the one to whom you owe a debt will forgive you ten thousand talents, in keeping with his greatness. He will not charge you interest or additional charges.”
If you are willing and forgive, then the one who presents prayers takes your offering and brings it up with him. But if you do not forgive,
he says this to you: “I will not present an unclean offering before the holy throne. But look, you yourself are coming there
to give an account to the one to whom you owe a debt, and you will bring your offering with you.” Then he leaves your offering and goes away.
Listen to what the prophet says: “Cursed is anyone who has a good male in his flock, but makes a vow and sacrifices a sick animal to the Lord.”
For he says, “Offer it to your governor! Will he be pleased with you or show you favor?” Therefore you must forgive your debtor before your prayer,
and then pray. When you pray, your prayer will rise up before God and will not be left on the earth.
For he says through the prophet, “This is my rest: give rest to the weary.” So do what pleases God, O human being, and you will have no need to say, “Forgive me.”
Give rest to the weary, visit the sick, and provide for the poor: this is prayer. I assure you of this, my dear friend:
Whenever someone does what pleases God, that itself is prayer. For it is written that when Zimri committed sexual immorality with the Midianite woman,
Phinehas son of Eleazar saw him, entered the chamber, and killed them both. His killing them was counted as prayer for him.
For this is what David said about him: “Phinehas stood up and prayed, and it was counted to him as righteousness, from generation to generation and forever.”
The killing of those whom he killed for the sake of his God was counted as prayer for him. Take care, my dear friend, lest an opportunity arise for you to do something that satisfies God's will,
and you say, “The time for prayer is near. I will pray, and then I will attend to it.” While you are trying to finish your prayer, the opportunity to give relief may slip away from you,
and you will fall short of God's will and pleasure, and incur sin through your prayer. Instead, do what pleases God, and that is prayer.
Listen to what the apostle said: “If we judged ourselves, we would not be judged.” Judge for yourself what I am telling you.
Suppose you happen to be traveling on a long journey, and thirst overtakes you in the heat, and you turn aside to one of the brothers,
and say to him, “Relieve me from the torment of thirst,” and he says to you, “It is time for prayer. I will pray, and then come to you.”
While he prays and comes to you, you die of thirst. Which seems better to you: that he should go and pray, or that he should relieve your suffering?
Or suppose you are traveling on a journey in winter, and rain and snow fall on you, and you are chilled and suffering,
and again you turn aside to your friend at the time for prayer, and he answers you with the same words, and you die of the cold. What benefit is there in his prayer,

since he gave no relief to someone suffering? For when our Lord gave a picture of the time of judgment, when he separated people and placed them on his right and on his left, he said to those on his right:
“I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me a drink; I was sick, and you visited me; I was a stranger, and you took me in.”
He spoke in similar terms to those on his left. Because they had not done these things, he sent them away to torment, while he sent those on his right into the kingdom.
Prayer is beautiful, and its deeds are good. Prayer is accepted when relief is found in it, and prayer is heard when forgiveness is found in it.
Prayer is loved when it is pure of all deceit, and prayer is powerful when God's power is fulfilled in it.
As for what I have written to you, my dear friend—that a person should do God's will, and that this itself is prayer—it seems to me
that this is good. But do not neglect prayer because I have told you this. Instead, be even more diligent in prayer,
and do not grow weary, as it is written that our Lord said, “Keep praying, and do not grow weary.” Be diligent and watchful,
and put sleepiness and sluggishness far from you. Keep watch by day and by night, and do not lose heart.
I will show you the times for prayer. For there are petition, thanksgiving, and praise. Petition is when a person asks for mercy for their sins;
thanksgiving is when you give thanks to your Father in heaven; and praise is when you praise him for his works. When you are in distress, offer a petition.
And when you are sustained by his good gifts, give thanks to the giver. And when your mind rejoices, offer praise.
And offer all your prayers before God with discernment. See how David too always spoke this way: “I rose
to thank you for your righteous judgments.” In another psalm he also said, “Praise the Lord from the heavens; praise him in the heights.” Again he said,
“I will bless the Lord at all times, and his praises will always be in my mouth.” He did not pray in just one manner, but with discernment.
And I, my dear friend, am convinced of this: God gives people whatever they ask for with care.
But he takes no pleasure in someone who makes an offering carelessly. As it is written, this, then, is required of the one who prays when offering prayer: he must inspect his offering carefully,
in case a blemish is found in it, and then offer it, so that your offering does not remain on the earth. And what is the offering if not prayer,
as I wrote to you above? For David said, “Offer thanksgiving as a sacrifice to the Lord, and fulfill your vows to the Most High.”
For pure prayer is better than all offerings. Therefore, my dear friend, devote yourself to prayer, which speaks on your behalf
with God, as it is written in Isaiah the prophet, when he made the people of Israel aware of their sins and called them rulers of Sodom,
instead of the children he had raised and exalted. They had exchanged their honor for disgrace. Earlier Isaiah said about them, “I raised and exalted children,”
and further on he said, “Rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah.” And when they did not listen to the voice of the prophet, who said about them
that their land was devastated and their cities were burning with fire, and called them rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah,
then they took their offerings and brought them so that they might be forgiven. But their offerings were not accepted, because their wickedness was great,
as with the household of Eli the priest. For Scripture says that the wickedness of Eli’s household will not be atoned for by sacrifices and offerings.
A similar pronouncement also went out against the people of Israel. For Isaiah said to them, “What use to me are your many sacrifices? says the Lord.
I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams and the fat of fattened animals, and I have no desire for the blood of bulls and goats. Who,” he said, “asked for these things from your hands?”
And they said to him, “But why, since you asked for them? And why are our offerings not accepted?” For the prophet said to them, “Because your hands are full of blood.”
They said to him, “What remedy is there for us?” He said to them, “Wash yourselves and become clean. Remove your evil deeds from before my eyes.
Stop doing evil and learn to do good. Seek justice and do good to the oppressed. Give justice to orphans and give justice to widows.”
They said to the prophet, “And when we have done these things, what will happen to us?” He said to them, “This is what the Lord says:
When you have done these things, come, let us speak with one another.” And how do human beings speak with God except through prayer,
when it has no blemish? Prayer that has a blemish does not speak with God, as it is written in that passage, where he said,
“Even if you multiply your prayers, I will not listen, because your hands are full of blood.” And he said to them, “When you have washed yourselves and we have spoken together,
even if your sins are like scarlet, I will make them white as snow; and even if they are red like crimson, they will become like wool.”
If you are willing and listen to me, you will eat the good things of the land. But if you are unwilling and resist, you will be ravaged / devoured by the sword. The mouth of the Lord has spoken.
Oh, the glorious mysteries that Isaiah foresaw! For he said to them, “Your hands are full of blood.” What is this blood that Isaiah foresaw?
It is none other than the blood of Christ, which they took upon themselves and their children, and the blood of the prophets whom they killed. This is the blood that became red like scarlet
and like crimson, and stained them. They cannot be cleansed unless they wash in the water of baptism and receive the body and blood of Christ.
Blood is atoned for by blood, the body is cleansed by the body, sins are washed away with water, and prayer speaks with the Majesty.
See, my beloved, that sacrifices and offerings have been rejected, and prayer has been chosen in their place. From now on, love pure prayer and labor in supplication.
At the beginning of all your prayers, pray your Lord’s prayer. Be diligent in everything I have written to you, and whenever you pray, remember your friend.
The Demonstration on Prayer is finished.
Demonstration on Wars
This thought came to me at this time concerning the upheaval that is about to take place at this time, and the army that has gathered itself for war.
The times are determined beforehand and appointed by God. Times of peace are fulfilled in the days of good and righteous people,
and times in which evils abound are fulfilled in the days of wicked and unjust people. For it is written:
“Good is destined to come, and blessed is the one through whom it comes. Evil is destined to come, but woe to the one through whom it comes.”
Good came to God’s people, and the blessing remains with the one through whom the good came. And evil was stirred up against the assembled army
by a wicked and arrogant man who boasts. Woe also lingers there, with the one through whose hands evil is stirred up.
But do not blame the wicked man, my beloved, for bringing evil upon many, because the times are determined beforehand and appointed, and the time of their fulfillment has arrived.
Now, because this is an evil time, understand in a veiled sense what I am writing to you. For it is written: “What is exalted among human beings
is detestable before God.” Again it is written: “Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and everyone who humbles himself will be exalted.” Jeremiah also said:
“Let the mighty man not boast in his might, nor the rich man in his wealth.” The blessed apostle also said: “Let the one who boasts boast in the Lord.”
David said: “I saw the wicked man exalted and towering like a cedar of Lebanon. But when I passed by, he was gone. I looked for him but could not find him.”
Everyone who boasted was humbled. Cain exalted himself over his brother Abel and killed him. He was cursed and became trembling and wandering on the earth.
Again, the people of Sodom exalted themselves over Lot, and fire fell upon them from heaven and burned them up.
Their city was overturned upon them. Esau exalted himself over Jacob and persecuted him, and Jacob received Esau’s birthright and blessings.
Jacob’s sons exalted themselves over Joseph, and they fell down and bowed before him in Egypt. Pharaoh exalted himself over Moses and his people.
Pharaoh drowned in the sea, he and his army. Dathan and Abiram exalted themselves over Moses, and they went down alive to Sheol.
Goliath threatened David, but he fell before him and was shattered. Saul also pursued David, but he fell by the sword of the Philistines.
Absalom rose up against him, but Joab killed him in battle. Ben-hadad also boasted against Ahab, but he was delivered into Israel’s hands.
Sennacherib blasphemed against Hezekiah and his God, but his army became dead bodies when one of the watchers went out and slaughtered
185,000 in his camp, through Hezekiah’s prayer, through the prayer of Isaiah the prophet, the glorious one among the prophets.
Ahab rose up against Micaiah, but he went up and fell at Ramoth-gilead. Jezebel boasted against Elijah, but dogs ate her on the estate of Jezreel.
Haman boasted against Mordecai, but his wrongdoing came back upon his own head. The Babylonians boasted against Daniel and threw him into the lions’ den.
Daniel came up victorious, and they fell into the den in his place. Again, the Babylonians boasted and slandered Hananiah and his companions.
They fell into the fiery furnace and came up victorious, while the flame consumed their slanderers.
For Nebuchadnezzar said, “I will ascend to heaven and raise my throne above the stars of God. I will sit on the lofty mountains in the far reaches of the north.”
Isaiah said about him, “Because your heart has made you so proud, you will now be brought down to Sheol, and everyone who sees you will be astonished at you.”
Sennacherib also spoke this way: “I will ascend to the mountain heights, even to the far reaches of Lebanon. I will dig and drink water,
and with my horses’ hooves I will dry up all the deep rivers.” Because he had become so proud, Isaiah himself also said about him:
“Does an axe boast against the one who chops with it? Does a saw exalt itself over the one who saws with it? Does a rod lift itself up against the one who raises it?”
“You, Sennacherib,” he says, “are an axe in the hands of the one who chops, a saw in the hands of the one who saws, and a rod in the hand of the one who raises it to discipline.
You are a staff for striking. You were sent against a perverse people, and you were also commissioned against a wrathful people,
to take captives and seize plunder. You made all human beings and all nations like the mud of the streets.
When you had done all these things, why did you exalt yourself over the one who holds you, boast against the one who saws with you, and revile the city of the Holy One?
You said to the people of Jerusalem, ‘Can your God rescue you from my hands?’ And you dared to say,
‘Who is the Lord, that he should rescue you from my hands?’ Therefore hear the word of the Lord, who says, ‘I will shatter the Assyrian in my land,
and on my mountains I will trample him.’” When he was shattered and trampled, the virgin daughter of Zion despised him, and the daughter of Jerusalem shook her head
and said, “Whom have you reviled and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice? You have lifted your eyes on high against the Holy One of Israel.
Through your messengers you have reviled the Lord. Now see: a ring has been put in your nose and a bridle on your lips.

You have returned with a broken heart, though you came with a proud heart.” His death came at the hands of his loved ones, and there, in the house where he placed his trust, he was overthrown and fell before his god.
It was indeed fitting, my beloved, that this sacrifice and offering should be before that very god in whom he trusted. In his house of worship, his corpse became a memorial to his idol.
Again, the ram became proud and exalted itself. It charged westward, northward, and southward, and subdued many beasts.
And none stood before it until the male goat came from the west, struck the ram, and broke its horns. It brought the ram very low.
Now the ram is the king of Media and Persia, namely Darius, and the male goat is Alexander, son of Philip the Macedonian.
For Daniel saw the ram while he was in the east, before the gate of Susa the citadel, in the city of Elam,
by the river Ulai. It was charging westward, northward, and southward, and none of the animals could stand before it.
The male goat came out from the city of the Greeks and rose up against the ram. It struck it and broke both its horns, the large one and the small one.
Why does he say that it broke both its horns? Because it brought low both the kingdoms that he ruled:
the smaller one of the Medes and the larger one of the Persians. When Alexander the Greek came, he killed Darius, king of Media and Persia.
For this is what the angel said to Daniel when explaining the vision to him: “The ram that you saw is the king of Media and Persia, and the male goat is the king of the Greeks.”
For from the time when both the ram’s horns were broken until the present time, there have been six hundred and forty-eight years.
So the ram’s horns are broken, and though its horns are broken, look: it exalts itself and rises up against the fourth beast,
which is strong and mighty, whose teeth are iron and whose claws are bronze. It devours [?] and crushes, and whatever remains it tramples with its feet.
O ram whose horns are broken, leave the beast alone and do not provoke it, lest it devour you and crush you. The ram could not stand before the male goat;
how can it stand before the terrifying beast? Its mouth speaks boastful things, and whatever it finds, it crouches over, like a lion over its prey.
Whoever provokes the lion becomes its portion, and whoever rouses the beast, it devours. Whoever goes and falls beneath the beast’s feet, it tramples.
For the beast will not be killed until the Ancient of Days sits upon the throne, and the Son of Man approaches before him and is given authority.
Then that beast will be killed and its body destroyed. The kingdom of the Son of Man will be an everlasting kingdom, and his authority will endure for all generations.
Be still, you who exalt yourself; do not boast. For if your wealth has made your heart proud, it is not greater than Hezekiah’s,
which, because he boasted of it before the Babylonians, was all taken away from him and carried to Babylon. And if you boast of your sons,
they will be taken away from you to the beast, just as the sons of King Hezekiah were taken away and became eunuchs in the palace of the king of Babylon.
And if you boast of your wisdom, you are not superior to the ruler of Tyre, whom Ezekiel rebuked, saying to him,
“Are you wiser than Daniel? Or have you seen hidden things through your wisdom?” And if your mind has become proud because of your many years, they are not as numerous
as those of the ruler of Tyre, who ruled the kingdom during the days of twenty \and two kingdoms/and two kings/ of the house of Judah,
whose years amounted to four hundred and forty years. And when the years of the king of Tyre had increased by all this time, he said in his heart,
“I am God, and I sit in the seat of God in the heart of the seas.” But Ezekiel said to him, “You are a human being, and you are not God.”
For when the ruler of Tyre walked blamelessly among the stones of fire, mercy was shown to him. But when his heart became proud, the overshadowing cherub destroyed him.
And what, then, are the stones of fire, if not the children of Zion and the children of Jerusalem? For in earlier times,
in the days of David and his son Solomon, Hiram was a friend of the house of Israel. But when they were taken captive from their country,
he gloated over them and stamped his foot, and did not remember his friendship with the house of David. And when I said that the children of Judah were called stones of fire,
I did not say this from my own imagination. Rather, Jeremiah the prophet said it about them. For when he mourns for them in his Lamentations, he says,
“The children of Zion were more precious than precious stones.” And again he says, “How the stones of the sanctuary are scattered at the head of every street!”
And again he says in the prophet, “They were holy stones scattered in his land.” And these very stones—
fire was burning in them, as Jeremiah said: “The word of the Lord was in my heart like fire burning and shut up in my bones.”
And again he said to Jeremiah, “Look, I am making my word in your mouth fire, and this people will be like wood.” And again he said, “My words go out like fire,
and like iron that cuts stone.” For this reason Hiram, the ruler of Tyre, walked among the prophets, who were called stones of fire.
And again he said to him, “You were with the anointed, sheltering cherub.” For the king was called a cherub, since he was anointed with holy oil,
and he sheltered all his people. As Jeremiah said, “The breath of our nostrils, the Lord’s anointed, of whom we said, ‘In his shade we will live among the nations.’”
For they lived in the king’s shade while he stood at their head. But when the crown of their head fell, they were left without shade.
And if anyone says that this statement refers to Christ, let him accept what I write to him without argument, and so be convinced
that it refers to the king. For Jeremiah said on behalf of the people, “Woe to us, for the crown of our head has fallen!” But Christ did not fall,
because he rose on the third day. It was the king who fell from the house of Judah, and their kingdom was never established again.
And as for his further statement that the sheltering cherub destroyed him: the cherub who destroyed him was Nebuchadnezzar, as it is written, “He performed labor against Tyre,
but no wages were given to him from Tyre for his army.” And in return for his labor against Tyre, the land of Egypt was given to him.
But why were no wages from Tyre given to Nebuchadnezzar? It was because its wealth went away by sea, and Nebuchadnezzar did not take it.
And at that very time the sheltering cherub, who is Nebuchadnezzar, destroyed him. For there were two cherubim: one anointed and sheltering,
and one sheltering but not anointed. For earlier he said, “You were with the anointed, sheltering cherub,” but later he said, “The sheltering cherub destroyed you,”
and did not say “anointed.” For Nebuchadnezzar was not anointed, but David and Solomon were, as were the other kings who came after them.
And how was Nebuchadnezzar called “sheltering”? It was through the vision of the tree, when he saw a tree in the middle of the earth, beneath which all the wild animals lived,
and on whose branches all the birds of the sky nested, and from which all flesh was fed. When Daniel interpreted his dream for him,
Daniel said to him, “You are the tree, that tree you saw in the middle of the earth, and beneath you all the nations live.”
For this reason he was the sheltering cherub who destroyed the ruler of Tyre, because he had gloated over the children of Israel when they were taken captive from their land.
And because his heart became proud, Tyre too lay in ruins for seventy years, like Jerusalem, which lay in ruins for seventy years.
For Isaiah said about her, “Tyre will be forgotten for seventy years, like the days of one king, and she will prostitute herself with all the kingdoms on the face of the earth.”
You who exalt yourself and lift yourself up, do not let the pride of your heart deceive you, so that you say, “I will advance against a fertile land and against a mighty beast.”
For the beast will not be killed by the ram when its horns are broken. For the male goat broke the ram’s horns.
Now the male goat has become a mighty beast, because when the descendants of Japheth took possession of the kingdom, they killed Darius, king of Persia.
Now the fourth beast has swallowed the third. The third is the descendants of Japheth, and the fourth is the descendants of Shem,
who are the descendants of Esau. For when Daniel saw the vision of the four beasts, he saw first the one belonging to the descendants of Ham, the offspring of Nimrod, who are the Babylonians;
and second, the one belonging to the Persians and Medes, who are descendants of Japheth; and third, the one belonging to the Greeks, the brothers of the Medes;
and fourth, the one belonging to the descendants of Shem, who are the descendants of Esau. For there was an alliance between the descendants of Japheth and the descendants of Shem.
Rule was taken away from the descendants of Japheth the younger and given to Shem the elder. It remains so to this day, and will forever.
But when the time comes for the rule of the descendants of Shem to end, the ruler who came from the descendants of Judah will receive the kingdom, when he comes at his second coming.
For in the vision that Nebuchadnezzar saw, which Daniel made known and explained to Nebuchadnezzar, he saw a statue standing before him.
The statue’s head was gold, its chest and arms were silver, its belly and thighs were bronze, and its legs and feet were iron and earthenware.
Daniel said to Nebuchadnezzar, “You are the head of gold.” And why was he called the head of gold? It was because Jeremiah’s word was fulfilled concerning him.
For Jeremiah said, “Babylon is a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, making the whole earth drink from its wine.”
Babylon was also called the head of all kingdoms, as it is written: “Babylon was the beginning of Nimrod’s kingdom.”
And he said that the statue’s chest and arms were silver. He was pointing to a kingdom inferior to his, that of Darius the Mede.
For he received the kingdom by weighing. The kingdom of the house of Nimrod was weighed and found wanting, and Darius received it in its deficient state.
For this reason he said that his kingdom was inferior. And because it was deficient, the descendants of Media did not rule over the whole earth. The statue’s belly and thighs were bronze.
And when he said that the third kingdom would rule over the whole earth, this is the kingdom of the descendants of Javan, who are descendants of Japheth.
For the descendants of Javan rose against the kingdom of their brothers, because Madai and Javan are sons of Japheth. But Madai was foolish and lacked the ability to govern a kingdom,
until his brother Javan, who was wise and crafty, came to destroy the kingdom. For Alexander son of Philip ruled over the whole earth.
The statue’s legs and feet were iron. This is the kingdom of the descendants of Shem, who are the descendants of Esau,
which is strong as iron. And he said, “Just as iron crushes and pulverizes everything, so the fourth kingdom will crush and subdue everything.”
And he explained concerning the feet and toes, some of which were iron and some earthenware made of clay. For he said that in this way they would mingle through human offspring.
And they will not cling to one another, just as iron does not mix with clay. He showed this concerning the fourth kingdom.
For in the kingdom of the descendants of Esau, it was not a king's son who would arise as king to govern the kingdom.
Rather, when the descendants of Esau gathered in the strong city and established a senate, they would appoint from there a head of the city,
a wise man to govern the kingdom, so that when the ruler of their kingdom weighed them, they would not be found wanting,
and the kingdom would not be taken away from them, as the kingdom of the descendants of boastful Nimrod was taken away and given to the descendants of foolish Media.
And the king who arose would destroy the offspring of the king before him, and they did not cling to one another. But as for the human seed that was compared to clay,
this is how the matter stands: whenever a king was chosen for the kingdom, he became mixed with the root of the kingdom of iron.
And he showed that in the days of those kings who hold power in the kingdom, the God of heaven would establish a kingdom that would never be destroyed
or pass away. This is the kingdom of the Messiah the King, which will bring the fourth kingdom to an end. And above he said,
"You saw a stone cut out without hands, and it struck the statue on its feet of iron and pottery and crushed them completely."
He did not say that it struck the statue on its head, or on its chest and arms, or on its belly and thighs, but on its feet.
For of the whole statue, it is only the feet that the stone finds when it comes. And in the following verse he said that the iron and bronze were crushed together,
along with the silver and gold. For after them, when the Messiah the King reigns, he will then bring down the fourth kingdom and crush the whole statue.
For the statue was identified as the whole world: its head was Nebuchadnezzar; its chest and arms were the king of Media and Persia; and its belly and thighs were the king of the Greeks.
Its legs and feet were the kingdom of the descendants of Esau. And the stone that struck the statue and crushed it, and with which the whole earth was filled,
is the kingdom of the Messiah the King, who will abolish the kingdom of this world and reign forever and ever.
Listen again concerning the vision of the four beasts that Daniel saw coming up from the sea, each different from the others.
This was their appearance: the first was like a lion and had the wings of an eagle. And I saw that its wings were plucked out,
and it stood on its feet like a human being, and a human heart was given to it. The second beast resembled a bear, and it stood on one side,
with three ribs in its mouth between its teeth. The third beast was like a leopard, and it had four wings and four heads.
The fourth beast was terrifying, strong, and exceedingly powerful, and it had large teeth. It devoured and crushed, and whatever was left it trampled with its feet.
For the great sea that Daniel saw is the world, and these four beasts are the four kingdoms described above.
For he said of the first beast that it resembled a lion and had the wings of an eagle. The first beast is the kingdom of Babylon,
which resembles a lion. For Jeremiah wrote as follows: "Israel is a wandering sheep; lions have led them astray. First the king of Assyria devoured him,
and this last one, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, grew stronger than he." Jeremiah called him a lion and said that he had the wings of an eagle.
For this is what is written: When Nebuchadnezzar went out into the wilderness with the wild animals, his hair grew like an eagle’s. And he said, “I saw that its wings were plucked out.”
“It stood on its feet like a human being, and a human heart was given to it.” For first, in the vision of the statue, he was represented by gold,
which is more precious than anything used in the world. And in the vision of the beasts, he was represented by a lion, whose strength surpasses that of all the wild animals.
He was also represented by an eagle, which surpasses all the birds. What was written about him was fulfilled in him. For the Lord said about him:
“I myself have placed an iron yoke on the necks of all the nations, and they will serve the king of Babylon for seventy years.
I have also given him the wild animals and the birds of the sky to serve him.” For when he was king, represented by the head of gold, human beings served him
as a king. And when he went out into the wilderness, the wild animals served him as a lion. And when his hair became like an eagle’s,
the birds of the sky served him as an eagle. And when his heart became proud and he did not acknowledge that his authority had been given to him from heaven,
his iron yoke was broken off the necks of human beings, and he went out among the wild animals. Instead of a king’s heart, he was given a lion’s heart.
And when he was exalted above the wild animals, the lion’s heart was taken away from him, and he was given a bird’s heart. And when wings like an eagle’s grew on him,
he was exalted above the birds. Then his wings too were plucked out, and he was given a humble heart.
And when he acknowledged that the Most High rules over the kingdom of humanity and gives it to whomever he wishes, then he offered praise like a human being.
Of the second beast he said that it resembled a bear and stood on one side, because when the kingdom of Media and Persia arose,
it arose in the east. And there were three ribs in its mouth, because the ram was charging toward the west, the north, and the south,
toward three directions of heaven. It held these three directions and charged, corresponding to the three ribs in the bear’s mouth,
until the male goat came out from the west, struck the ram, and removed the ribs from its mouth.
Of the third beast he said that it resembled a leopard, and it had four bird’s wings on its sides, and that beast had four heads.
For the third beast is Alexander the Macedonian, because he was strong like a leopard. And the four wings and four heads that the beast had
were because he gave the kingdom to four of his friends to govern after him, when he came and killed Darius and reigned in his place.
And of the fourth beast he said that it was terrifying, mighty, and exceedingly strong. It devoured and crushed, and whatever remained it trampled with its feet.
It is the kingdom of the descendants of Esau, because after Alexander the Macedonian had reigned, the kingdom of the Greeks arose,
although Alexander himself was also one of the Greeks. But the vision of the third beast was fulfilled in him,
although the third and the fourth are one. Alexander reigned for twelve years.
The Greek kings who came after Alexander numbered seventeen kings, and the years of their reigns amounted to two hundred and sixty-nine years,
from Seleucus Nicanor to Ptolemy. And there were Caesars from Augustus to Philip Caesar.
Twenty-seven kings, whose years amount to two hundred and ninety-three years, and the eighteen years of Severus.
For Daniel said, “I was considering the ten horns on the beast’s head.” For the ten horns—
ten kings arose in that period, up to Antiochus. And he said that a little horn came up among these ten,
and three fell before it. For when Antiochus came to power, he brought down three kings and exalted himself against the holy ones of the Most High.
He entered Jerusalem, defiled the sanctuary, and put an end to sacrifices and offerings for a week and half a week,
which amount to ten and a half years. He brought prostitutes into the Lord’s house, abolished the observances prescribed in the Law, and killed righteous people,
handing them over to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth. For in his days the words spoken by David were fulfilled: “O God, the nations have entered your inheritance,
and defiled your holy temple. They have made Jerusalem a ruin. They have given the corpses of your servants as food to the birds of the sky,
and the flesh of your righteous ones to the beasts of the earth. They have poured out their blood like water around Jerusalem, and there is no one to bury them.”
For this was fulfilled at that time, when Eleazar, an old man advanced in years, was killed, along with the sons of blessed Shmuni,
who were seven in number, and when Judas and his brothers were fighting on behalf of their people while living in hiding.
At that time the horn waged war against the holy ones, and their strength was exhausted. Antiochus, that wicked man, spoke words against the Most High,
changed times and seasons, abolished Abraham’s covenant, and did away with the Sabbath rest. For he commanded the Jews not to practice circumcision.
For this reason he said of him, “He will intend to change times, seasons, and laws, and they were given into his hand
until a time, times, and half a time,” that is, a time and half a time: a week and a half, which amount to ten and a half years.
He also said, “The court sat, and they took his authority away from him, to destroy and annihilate him until the end of the kingdom.”
For judgment came upon Antiochus, judgment from heaven, and he fell ill with a severe and terrible disease. Because of the stench of his decay,
no one would come near him, as worms crawled out of him and ate his flesh, because he had oppressed the worm of Jacob.
His flesh rotted while he was still alive, because he had caused the corpses of Jerusalem’s people to rot without burial. He became unclean in his own eyes,
because he had defiled God’s sanctuary. He prayed but was not heard, because he had not heard the groaning of the righteous people he killed.
For he wrote a letter and sent it to the Jews, calling them “my friends.” But God had no mercy on him, and he died in his torment.
He also said that the holy ones of the Most High would receive the kingdom. What shall we say about this? Did the Israelites receive the kingdom of the Most High?
Certainly not! Or did that people come on the clouds of heaven? This has passed away from them. For Jeremiah said of them,
“Call them rejected silver, because the Lord has rejected them.” He also said that he would no longer look upon them. And Isaiah said of them,
“Depart, depart, and do not come near the unclean.” But concerning the holy ones of the Most High, he said this about them: “They will inherit the kingdom forever and ever.”
For they had a little rest from the exactions of kings and rulers after the death of Antiochus,
until the sixty-two weeks were completed. The Son of Man came to free them and gather them together, but they did not receive him.
For he came to receive fruit from them, but they gave him none, because their vines came from the vine of Sodom
and from the planting of Gomorrah. For thorns grew in the vineyard, and it bore wild grapes. Their wine became vinegar, and their fruit became gall.
Thorns cannot be softened, nor does vinegar return to the nature of wine, nor does gall change to a sweet nature.
For Isaiah had already appointed judges over them, men from Judah among whom a new and beloved plant had been planted.
These judges are those who sit on twelve thrones and judge their twelve tribes.
And he said to the judges: “Judge between me and my vineyard. What more was there, O judges,
to do for my vineyard that I have not done for it? Look, I planted it with vine shoots, but they became a foreign vine. I surrounded it with a hedge—the watchers of heaven.
I built its tower—the holy temple. I dug its winepress—the baptism of the priests. I sent rain down upon it—the words of my prophets.
I pruned and cultivated it, clearing away the deeds of the Amorites. I waited for it to produce grapes—righteousness—but it produced wild grapes—wickedness and sin.
I waited for justice, but there was plunder; for righteousness, but there was wailing. Hear, O judges, what I will do to my vineyard.
I will break down its hedge, and it will be trampled. I will tear down its tower, and it will be plundered. I will make it a wasteland because it produced wild grapes.
It will not be cultivated or pruned. Thorns and brushwood will grow in it, and I will command the clouds not to send rain down upon it.”
For the watchers of heaven withdrew from the vineyard’s hedge, and the tower, their strong refuge, was torn down.
The winepress, the cleansing of their sins, was overthrown. When the vine was unblemished, it was not fit for any work. Now that fire has consumed it and it is ruined,
how can it be fit for work? Fire consumed its two branches, and its middle was ruined. For its two branches are the two kingdoms,
and its ruined middle is Jerusalem. Many servants were sent to them by the owner of the vineyard, and they killed them.
They sent no fruit to the owner of the vineyard. After the servants, the beloved son was sent to receive fruit from them and bring it to the one who sent him.
They seized him and took him outside the vineyard. They cut pegs from the vineyard’s stakes and drove them into his hands. He was hungry and asked them for food.
They took gall from the vineyard’s fruit and gave it to him. He was thirsty and asked them for a drink. They gave him vinegar, but he would not drink it.
They wove together thorns that had grown in the vineyard and placed them on the head of the vineyard owner’s son. For from the time the vineyard came into being,
these were the fruits it displayed. Its owner uprooted it and threw it into the fire. He planted good vines in the vineyard, which bear fruit and make the cultivator glad.
For Christ is the vineyard, and his Father is the cultivator. The vines are those who drink from his cup. From then on, one vineyard took the place of another.
And at his coming he handed over the kingdom to the Romans, who were called the descendants of Esau. These descendants of Esau are keeping the kingdom for the one who gave it.
And the holy people, chosen in place of the people, inherited an everlasting kingdom. For he made them jealous through a people that was no people, and angered them through a foolish people.
And he set the holy people free. For behold, the whole covenant of God is exempt from the taxes of kings and rulers.
For even if someone serves pagans, the moment he joins God's covenant he is set free. But the Jews serve as slaves among the nations.
For this is what he said about the holy ones: that they would inherit the kingdom beneath heaven. For if he spoke about them,
why do they serve as slaves among the nations? And if they say that it has not happened yet, but that the kingdom given to the Son of Man is still to come—
is it heavenly or earthly? And behold, the children of the kingdom have been marked and have received their freedom from this world.
For although it exists now, it does not wish to be subjected to the army of the king who comes and takes its kingdom. Rather, it keeps his hostages in honor,
because when he comes he abolishes the kingdom, so that he may not come against them in anger. For when the one to whom the kingdom belongs comes,
at his second coming, he takes back what he gave. And he becomes king forever and ever, and his kingdom does not pass away, because his kingdom is everlasting.
For long ago he gave the kingdom to the descendants of Jacob and subjected the descendants of Esau to them, as Isaac said to Esau:
"You will serve your brother Jacob." And when they no longer proved worthy of kingship, he took it away from the descendants of Jacob
and gave it to the descendants of Esau, until the one to whom it belongs comes. They will hand over the deposit to the one who gave it and will not defraud him of it.
And the keeper of the kingdom will submit to him, to the one to whom everything submits. For this reason, this kingdom of the descendants of Esau
will not be delivered into the hands of the assembled armies that wish to attack it, because the kingdom is being kept for the one who gave it,
and he guards it. And concerning what I have written to you, my dear friend, that the kingdom of the descendants of Esau is being kept for the one who gave it, have no doubt
that this kingdom will not be defeated. For a mighty man whose name is Jesus has come in strength, and the whole army of the kingdom bears his armor.
Search and see: he too is registered with them for the poll tax. And just as he is registered with them for the poll tax, so he also helps them.
His standard is great in that land. They wear his armor and are not defeated in battle. And if you say to me, "Why, in the years of the kings before these,
did they defeat the beast and subjugate it?" It was because the leaders and kings who ruled at that time in the kingdom of the descendants of Esau
did not wish to take with them into battle the man registered with them for the poll tax. For this reason the beast was subjugated for a little while, but it was not killed.
But these things that I have written to you, my dear friend, concerning what is written in Daniel, I have not brought to completion, but have stopped short of completion.
And if anyone disputes them, tell him this: "These words are not sealed, because God's words have no limit
and are not sealed." For a foolish person says, "The words go only this far, and there is nothing more to add to them
or to take away from them." For God's wealth cannot be counted and has no limit. If you take water from the sea, its loss is not noticeable.
And if you take sand from its shore, its quantity is not diminished. And if you count the stars of heaven, you will not reach the end of them.
If you light a fire from a blaze, nothing is diminished. And if you receive some of the Spirit of Christ, Christ lacks nothing.
If Christ dwells in you, he is not wholly contained in you. And if the sun enters through the windows of your house, the whole sun has not reached you.
All these things that I have listed for you were created by the word of God. Therefore, know that no one has comprehended the word of God
or reached its limit. Therefore, do not argue about these things and say, “These are all there are, and that is enough.” Rather, listen to these things from me,
and inquire about them also among our brothers who share our faith. For anyone who mocks his brother’s words—even if he says, “My words are wise”—do not listen to his words.
As for what I wrote to you about these armies that are being stirred up for war, it was not because something had been revealed to me that I made these things known to you.
Rather, listen to the words at the beginning of the letter: everyone who exalted himself was humbled. For even if armies advance and conquer,
know that this is God’s discipline. And if they conquer, they are condemned by a just judgment. Nevertheless, know this:
the beast will be killed at its appointed time. But you, my brother, at this time be diligent in asking for mercy, so that there may be peace upon God’s people.
The Demonstration on Wars is finished.
Demonstration on the Members of the Covenant
The word that I speak is fitting and worthy of acceptance: we should wake from our sleep at this time
and lift our hearts along with our hands to God in heaven, lest the master of the house come suddenly, so that when he comes he may find us awake.
Let us await the appointed time of the glorious bridegroom, so that we may enter his bridal chamber with him. Let us prepare oil for our lamps, so that we may go out joyfully to meet him.
Let us prepare provisions for our lodging, for the road that is narrow and constricted. Let us strip off and throw away all our filth, so that we may put on clothes for the banquet.
Let us trade with the money we have received, so that we may be called diligent servants. Let us persevere in prayer, so that we may pass through the region of terror.
Let us cleanse our hearts of wrongdoing, so that we may see the Exalted One in his glory. Let us be merciful, as it is written, so that God may have mercy on us. Let there be peace among us,
so that we may be called brothers of Christ. Let us hunger for righteousness, so that we may be satisfied at the table of his kingdom. Let us be the salt of truth,
so that we may not become food for the serpent. Let us clear the thorns from what we sow, so that we may yield fruit a hundredfold. Let us set our building upon rock,
so that it may not be shaken by winds and waves. Let us be vessels for honorable use, so that our Lord may require us for his service. Let us sell all our possessions
and buy ourselves the pearl, so that we may become rich. Let us place our treasure in heaven, so that when we go there we may open it and enjoy it. Let us visit our Lord among the sick,
so that he may call us and we may stand at his right hand. Let us hate our own lives and love Christ, just as he loved us and was handed over for our sake.
Let us honor the Spirit of Christ, so that we may receive grace from him. Let us be strangers to the world, just as Christ was not of it.
Let us be meek and humble, so that he may give us the land of the living as our inheritance. Let us persevere in his service, so that he may serve us in the dwelling of the holy ones.
Let us pray his prayer in purity, so that it may enter before the Lord of majesty. Let us share in his suffering, so that we may also live in his resurrection.
Let us bear his mark on our bodies, so that we may escape the coming wrath. For the day on which he comes is terrible, and who can endure it?
He is vengeful, and his wrath is fierce, and he destroys all the wicked. Let us put the helmet of salvation on our heads, so that we are not struck down and killed in battle.
Let us gird our waists with truth, so that we are not found weak in the contest. Let us rise and awaken Christ, so that he may still the waves that beset us.
Let us take up a shield against the evil one: readiness in the good news of our Savior. Let us receive authority from our Lord to tread on snakes and scorpions.
Let us put anger away from us, along with all rage and malice. Let no insults come from our mouths, with which we pray to God.
Let us not be accursed, so that we may escape the curse of the law. Let us be diligent workers, so that we may claim our wages along with those who came first.
Let us bear the burden of the day, so that we may seek a greater reward. Let us not be idle workers, for our Lord has hired us for his vineyard.
Let us be planted like vines within his vineyard, for he is the true vineyard. Let us be good vines, so that we are not uprooted from the vineyard.
Let us be a sweet fragrance, so that our scent may spread to those around us. Let us be poor in the world and enrich many with our Lord’s teaching.
Let us call no one on earth our father, so that we may be children of the Father in heaven. Though we have nothing, we possess everything.
Though no one knows us, we have many acquaintances. Let us rejoice in our hope at all times, so that we may find joy in our hope and our Savior.
Let us judge ourselves justly and condemn ourselves, so that we do not hang our heads before the judges seated on thrones and judging the tribes.
Let us take up a weapon for battle: the readiness of the gospel. Let us knock at the gate of heaven, so that it may be opened before us and we may enter through it.
Let us ask boldly for mercy, so that we may receive all that we need. Let us seek his kingdom and his righteousness, so that we may receive what is added to us on earth.
Let us set our minds on the things above, the heavenly things, and meditate on them, where Christ has been raised and exalted. But let us leave behind the world, which is not ours.
So that we may reach the place to which we have been invited, let us lift our eyes to the heights, so that we may see the radiance being revealed. Let us raise our wings like eagles.
So that we may see the body wherever it is, let us prepare offerings for the King: desirable fruits, fasting and prayer.
Let us keep his pledge pure, so that he may entrust us with his entire treasury. For whoever deals falsely with his pledge is not allowed to enter the treasury.
Let us treat the body of Christ with care, so that our bodies may rise at the sound of the trumpet. Let us listen for the bridegroom’s voice, so that we may enter the bridal chamber with him.
Let us prepare a gift for his wedding feast and go out joyfully to meet him. Let us put on a holy garment and recline at the head of the chosen.
Whoever has not put on a banquet garment is cast into the outer darkness. Whoever asks to be excused from the banquet will not taste the supper.
Whoever loves estates and commerce is excluded from the city of the saints. Whoever does not bear fruit within the vineyard is uprooted and thrown into torment.
Whoever has received money from his master must return it to its giver with its profit. Whoever wishes to be a merchant should buy an estate and the treasure within it.
Whoever receives good seed should clear his land of thorns. Whoever wishes to be a fisherman should cast his net at all times.
Whoever is being trained as an athlete should guard himself from the world. Whoever wishes to receive a crown should run in the contest like a champion.
Whoever wants to enter the arena to fight should be trained to face his opponent. Whoever wants to enter battle should take up weapons to fight.
He should keep polishing them at all times. Whoever has taken on the likeness of angels should be a stranger to human society. Whoever has taken up the yoke of the holy ones,
let him keep buying and selling far from himself. Whoever seeks to gain his own soul should keep worldly possessions far from himself. Whoever loves the house in heaven,
let him not labor over a building of clay that will fall. Whoever expects to be caught up in the clouds should not provide himself with splendid mounts.
Whoever awaits the bridegroom’s feast should not love the feasting of this present time. Whoever wishes to enjoy the drink kept in reserve,
let him keep drunkenness far from himself. Whoever has prepared himself for the evening banquet should not make excuses and become a merchant. Whoever has had good seed fall within him,
let him not allow the evil one to sow weeds within him. Whoever has begun to build a tower should calculate all his expenses.
Whoever builds but lacks the means to finish must take care not to become a laughingstock to passersby. Whoever sets his building on rock,
let him make its foundations deep, so that it does not fall because of the waves. Whoever wishes to escape the darkness should walk while he has light.
Whoever fears having to flee in winter should prepare himself in summer. Whoever expects to enter into rest should prepare his provisions for the Sabbath.
Whoever asks his master for forgiveness should also forgive his own debtor. Whoever does not demand repayment of a hundred denarii has ten thousand talents forgiven him by his master.
Whoever deposits his master’s money with the bankers is not called an evil servant. Whoever loves humility becomes an heir in the land of the living.
Whoever desires to make peace becomes one of God’s children. Whoever knows his master’s will should do his will, so that he does not receive many blows.
Whoever cleanses his heart of deceit, his eyes will see the king in his beauty. Whoever receives the Spirit of Christ should adorn his inner person.
Whoever has been called God’s temple should cleanse his body of all impurity. Whoever grieves the Spirit of Christ,
he does not lift his head out of troubles. Whoever receives the body of Christ should guard his body against all impurity. Whoever has put off the old person,
let him not return again to his former deeds. Whoever has put on the new person should guard himself against all filth. Whoever has put on armor from the water,
let him not take off his armor, lest he be condemned. Whoever has taken up a shield against the evil one should guard himself against the arrows he shoots at him. Whoever loses heart,
his master takes no pleasure in him. Whoever reflects on his Lord’s law should not be distracted by the cares of this world. Whoever meditates on his Lord’s law,
he is like a tree planted beside water. Whoever places his trust in his Lord is likewise like a tree firmly rooted beside a stream.
Whoever trusts in a human being [?] receives the curses of Jeremiah. Whoever has been invited to meet the bridegroom should prepare himself. Whoever has lit his lamp,
let him not allow it to go out. Whoever awaits the shout should take oil in his vessel. Whoever watches at the door should await his master. Whoever loves virginity,
let him imitate Elijah. Whoever has taken up the yoke of the holy ones should sit in silence. Whoever loves stillness should await his Lord, the hope of life.
For our adversary is skilled, my beloved, and the one who fights against us is cunning. He prepares himself to confront the valiant and victorious, so that they may grow weak.
For the weak already belong to him, and he does not wage war against the captives he has taken. Whoever has wings flies away from him.
And the arrows he shoots at him do not reach him. Spiritual people see him as he fights, but his weapon has no power over their bodies.
None of the children of light fear him, because darkness flees before the light. And the children of the Good One do not fear the evil one.
For he has given him to them to trample underfoot. When he appears to them in the likeness of darkness, they themselves become light.
And when he crawls toward them like a snake, they themselves become salt, which he cannot eat. And if he appears to them in the likeness of an asp,
they themselves become like little children. And if he attacks them through the desire for food, they defeat him by fasting, as our Savior did.
And if he wants to fight them through the desire of the eyes, they lift their eyes to the heights of heaven. And if he wants to overcome them through enticement,
they do not give him a hearing. And if he wants to fight them openly, look: they stand against him clothed in armor.
And if he wants to attack them through sleep, they wake up and keep watch, sing, and pray. And if he entices them through possessions,
they give them to the poor. And if he approaches them as something sweet, they do not taste him, because they know that he is bitter.
And if he inflames them with desire for Eve, they live by themselves, and not with the daughters of Eve.
For he attacked Adam through Eve, and Adam was enticed in his immaturity. Again he attacked Joseph through his master's wife.
But Joseph recognized his deceit and would not give him a hearing. Through a woman he fought against Samson until he took away his Nazirite consecration.
Reuben was the firstborn of all his brothers, but through his father's wife he brought disgrace upon him. Aaron was the high priest in Israel,
but because of his sister Miriam he became jealous of Moses. Moses was sent to deliver the people from Egypt, and he took with him a counselor of hateful things.
And the Lord met Moses and sought to kill him, until he sent his wife back to Midian. David was victorious in all his battles,
but through a daughter of Eve he was found to have a blemish. Amnon was handsome and good-looking, but he bound him with desire for his sister, and Absalom killed him
because of the dishonor done to Tamar. Solomon became greater than all the kings of the earth, but in his old age his wives turned his heart astray.
Through Jezebel, the daughter of Ethbaal, Ahab's wickedness increased, and he became deeply defiled. Again he tested Job through his children and his possessions.
And when he could not gain power over him, he went and took up his weapon against him. He came, bringing with him a daughter of Eve, who had drowned Adam.
And through her mouth he told Job, the righteous man, to blaspheme God. But Job rejected his counsel. King Asa too
defeated the one accursed among the living when he wanted to attack him through his mother. For Asa recognized his deceit and removed his mother from her high position.
He cut down her idol and threw it away. John was greater than all the prophets, but Herod killed him because of the dancing of a daughter of Eve.
Haman was wealthy and third in rank under the king, and his wife advised him to destroy the Jews. Zimri was chief of the tribe of Simeon,
but Cozbi, a daughter of the chiefs of Midian, brought him to ruin. And because of one woman, twenty-four thousand Israelites fell in a single day.
For this reason, my brothers, every man of the covenant or holy man who loves the solitary life and wants a woman of the covenant like himself to live with him,
It is better for him, then, to marry a woman openly and not give himself over to lust. The same is also proper for a woman:
if she will not separate from a celibate man, let her marry a man openly. It is fitting for a woman to live with a woman,
and right for a man to live with a man. Any man who wishes to live in chastity should not have his wife living with him,
lest he return to his former nature and be counted an adulterer. So this counsel that I give myself is fitting, right, and good,
and I give it also to you, my beloved celibates who do not marry women, and virgins who do not marry men, and those who have loved chastity.
It is right, proper, and fitting that, even if a person suffers hardship, he should remain alone. This is the fitting way for him to live,
as it is written in Jeremiah the prophet: “It is good for a man to take up your yoke in his youth, and to sit alone and be silent,
because he has accepted your yoke upon himself.” For this is fitting, my beloved, for anyone who has taken up Christ’s yoke: to keep his yoke in purity.
For thus it is written, my beloved, concerning Moses: from the time the Holy One revealed himself to him, he too loved chastity.
And from the time he consecrated himself, his wife served him. But it is written thus: “Joshua son of Nun was Moses’ attendant from his youth.”
And again it is written of Joshua that he did not leave the tent. And in the tent of meeting he was not attended by a woman,
because the law did not permit women to enter the tent of meeting. Rather, even when they came to pray,
they would pray at the entrance of the tent of meeting and return. He also commanded the priests to remain chaste during the time of their service
and not to have sexual relations with their wives. It is also written of Elijah that sometimes he lived on Mount Carmel and sometimes by the brook Cherith.
He was attended by his disciple. And because his heart was in heaven, the birds of heaven brought him food.
And because he had taken on the likeness of the heavenly Watchers, those very Watchers brought him bread and water when he was fleeing from Jezebel.
And because he had set all his thoughts on heaven, he was caught up to heaven in a chariot of fire, and his dwelling was there forever.
Elisha also followed in his master’s footsteps. He lived in the Shunammite woman’s upper room and was attended by his disciple.
For the Shunammite woman said this: “The prophet of God is holy, and he passes our way continually.” For this was fitting for his holiness:
that we should make him an upper room with its furnishings. And what were the furnishings in Elisha’s upper room except a bed, a table,
a chair, and a lampstand only? And what shall we say about John, who did not even live among other people,
but preserved his virginity in purity and received the spirit of Elijah? The blessed apostle also said about himself and Barnabas:
“Do we not have the right to eat and drink, and also to take women around with us?” But he said, “It is neither fitting nor right.”
For this reason, our brothers, we know and see that from the beginning it was through a woman that the adversary gained access to humanity,
and through her he will carry his work through to the end. For she is Satan’s weapon, and with her he fights against the champions. For through her he sings at all times.
For she had been his harp from the first day. Because of her the curse of the law was imposed, and because of her the promise was made to death.
For she bears children in pain and hands them over to death. Because of her the earth was cursed to produce thorns and thistles. From now on,
with the coming of the child of blessed Mary, the thorns are uprooted, sweat is removed, the fig tree is cursed, and the dust is made salt.
The curse is nailed to the cross, the blade of the sword is removed from before the tree of life, and it is given as food to believers.
Paradise is promised to the blessed, to virgins and holy people, and the fruits of the tree of life are given as food to believers and virgins,
