and a righteous person, though dead, is alive to God. For this death is sleep, as David said: “I lay down and slept and awoke.”
Again Isaiah said, “Those who lie in the dust will awake.” And our Lord said about the daughter of the synagogue ruler, “The girl has not died,
but is only sleeping.” And concerning Lazarus he said to his disciples, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going to wake him.”
And the apostle said, “We will all sleep, but we will not all be changed.” Again he said, “Do not grieve over those who are asleep.”
But we ought to fear the second death, which is full of weeping and gnashing of teeth, sighs and sorrows, and which dwells in the outer darkness.
But blessed are the faithful and the righteous at that resurrection for which they wait, when they will awake and receive the good things promised to them.
And the wicked who do not believe in the resurrection—woe to them because of what is reserved for them! It would have been better for them if they did not rise,
as they believe. For a servant whose master has prepared a beating and chains for him does not want to wake up when he falls asleep,
because he knows that when morning comes and he wakes up, his master will beat him and bind him. But the good servant whose master has promised him gifts
looks forward to morning coming, so that he may receive gifts from his master. Even when he falls asleep, he sees in his dream
his master giving him what he promised him. He rejoices in his dream and is glad and happy. But the wicked person's sleep is not pleasant to him,
because he thinks, 'Look, morning is coming upon me!' His heart is broken in his dream. But the righteous sleep, and their sleep is pleasant to them, by day and by night.
They are unaware of the whole long night, and it seems like a single hour to them. Then, at the morning watch, they wake up and rejoice.
But sleep weighs upon the wicked, and they resemble a man lying with a severe, deep-seated fever,
who turns this way and that in his bed and is troubled throughout the night, which drags on for him. He fears the morning, when his master will condemn him.
Our faith, however, teaches this: when human beings die, they sleep this sleep,
and they do not know good from evil. The righteous do not receive what was promised them, nor do the wicked receive their evil punishment,
until the judge comes and separates the right from the left. Be convinced by what is written: until the judge sits
and the books are opened before him, and the good and evil deeds are read out, those who have done good receive good things from the Good One,
and those who have done evil receive evil things from the just judge. For toward the good he does not change his nature and become just,
because he justly condemns many. But toward the wicked he changes his nature in this world, for his goodness is swallowed up in justice,
and he becomes entirely just. Goodness does not join with justice toward them, just as goodness did not assist harm,
nor justice goodness. For goodness is far removed from judgment, while justice stirs up judgment. Whoever goodness draws near to
should turn toward it. It does not hand him over to justice, lest justice condemn him when it calls him to account for his shortcomings.
But whoever goodness is far from, justice brings to trial; at that trial he is condemned and goes to torment.
Now listen, my dear friend, to this proof that repayment comes at the end. For when the shepherd separated his flock and placed them on his right and on his left,
it was only after he had acknowledged the goodness of the good that he gave them the kingdom as their inheritance. And it was only after he had reproached the wicked and they had been condemned
that he sent them to torment. And those who sent messengers after the king and said, 'This man shall not be king over us'—
it is only after he has received the kingdom and returned that his enemies are slaughtered before him. And the workers who hurried and toiled in the vineyard
do not receive their wages until the work stops. And the merchants who received money—it is only when the owner of the money comes that he demands the interest.
And the virgins who are waiting for the bridegroom grow drowsy and sleep because he delays coming, until they hear the cry. Then they wake up and prepare their lamps.
The wise women enter, while the foolish women are kept outside. And those who ran in faith are not made perfect without us.
Understand from all these things, my dear friend, and be certain that no one has yet received his reward. For the righteous have not inherited the kingdom,
nor have the wicked gone to torment. The shepherd has not yet separated his flock. Look, the laborers are still toiling in the vineyard and have not yet received their wages.
The merchants are still trading with the money, and their master has not yet come to settle accounts. The king has gone to receive a kingdom
and has not yet returned a second time. And these virgins who are waiting for the bridegroom are still asleep until now.
They are waiting for the shout, and then they will wake. And the earlier ones who labored in faith are not made perfect until the later ones arrive.
But those whose understanding is childish say, “If no one has yet received his reward, why did the apostle say that when we depart from the body, we will be with our Lord?”
Remember, my dear friend, that I explained this matter to you in the Demonstration on the Solitaries: the spirit that the righteous receive goes to our Lord,
to its heavenly nature, until the time of the resurrection, when it comes to clothe itself in the body in which it dwelt. It constantly brings that body to remembrance before God
and urges the resurrection of the body in which it dwelt. As the prophet Isaiah said concerning the church from the nations, “Let them remain steadfast and stand,
those who bring you to remembrance before the Lord, and give them no rest.” But the wicked have no one to bring them to remembrance before the Lord,
because the Holy Spirit is far from them, for they have only the natural soul and are buried in that natural state.
Again, the teachings that are the evil one’s instruments stumble over the saying of our Lord: “No one has ascended to heaven except the one who descended from heaven, the Son of Man,
who was in heaven.” They say, “Look, our Lord has testified that an earthly body has not ascended to heaven.” The ignorant do not grasp the meaning of this.
For when our Lord explained things to Nicodemus, he did not grasp the meaning of the saying. Then our Lord said to him, “No one has ascended to heaven
and descended to tell you what is there. For if I have told you about things on earth and you do not believe,
how will you believe if I tell you about things in heaven? For look, no other witness has descended from there with me
to testify about the things in heaven so that you might believe. For Elijah ascended there, but he has not descended to testify with me, so that the testimony of two might be confirmed.”
But you, my dear friend, must have no doubt about the resurrection of the dead, because the living mouth has testified, “I put to death, and I bring to life.”

Both statements came from one mouth. Just as we are certain that he puts to death, and we see it, so it is certain and trustworthy that he brings to life. Accept what I have explained to you, and believe
that on the day of resurrection your body will rise whole, and you will receive from your Lord the reward for your faith. You will rejoice and delight in what you have believed.
The Demonstration on the Resurrection of the Dead is completed.
Demonstration on Humility
Humility is good at all times. It rescues from every affliction those who draw near to it, and its fruits are many.
Humility produces many good things. Integrity is born from it, and through it Noah found favor, and it saved him, as it is written:
To whom God said, “I have seen that you are righteous and blameless in this generation.” There are many testimonies to humility, for Scripture says:
“The humble will inherit the earth and live on it forever.” Again, Isaiah the prophet says, “On whom shall I look, and with whom shall I dwell, except the gentle and humble person
who trembles at my word?” Again it says, “Better is someone humble in spirit and lowly in his eyes than someone who captures a city.” Again it says:
“The righteousness of the blameless person goes before him.” And about Moses, the faithful man, it is written: “He was humbler than all the people on the face of the earth.”
For humility bears witness to the good things that come from the fear of God. Many, too, are the gifts that those who love him gain through humility.
When you seek compassion, it is found among the humble. Humility is the dwelling place of righteousness. Learning is found among the humble,
and their lips pour forth knowledge. Humility gives birth to wisdom and understanding. The humble possess composure. Modesty and patience,
when you seek them, are found in the humble person. An ascetic life is fitting and desirable for them. The humble person's speech is pleasant, his face is cheerful, and he smiles and rejoices.
Love befits the humble, for they know how to conduct themselves in it. The humble fast from every evil, and their faces are joyful because their hearts are good.
The humble person speaks, and it befits him. His lips smile, but his voice is not heard. The humble person fears quarrelling, because it is the offspring of jealousy.
When the humble person hears angry words, he stops his ears, and they do not enter his heart. The humble person's mind gives birth to every good thing,
and the faculties of his understanding ponder beautiful things. The humble person drinks learning like water, and it enters him like oil into his arteries.
The humble person is lowly, but his heart is raised to the heights above. Where his treasure is, there his thoughts dwell. His bodily eyes look toward the earth,

but the eyes of his understanding look toward the heights above. The humble person is always careful not to have any cause for reproach in his dealings with anyone. The humble person meditates on his Lord's law,
and from it he takes the medicine he needs. The humble person rejoices in his companion's good fortune and regards his friend as himself. The humble person approaches someone proud and arrogant,
and captures and wins over his whole mind. Humility tears down rebellious strongholds and turns back anger and hostility.
Jacob's humility overcame the anger of his brother Esau and of the four hundred men with him. And Joseph's humility overcame
the anger of his brothers, who were jealous of him and hated him. Moses triumphed through his humility and humbled all Pharaoh's pride. And David's humility overcame
the pride of Goliath, who threatened him in anger. Hezekiah's humility overcame all the threats of Sennacherib, who threatened and blasphemed.
Mordecai's humility overcame all Haman's arrogance. Through their humility, Daniel and his companions overcame the wicked men who slandered them.
The humble keep themselves free from envy, jealousy, and quarrelling. Pride is abhorrent in their eyes, and they take no part in harshness.
They keep falsehood far from themselves, and slander is foreign to them. They drive out hostility and cast it away,
because they are children of peace. They drive arrogance out from among them and cast it away, because they care about their good name. They know nothing of obstinacy,
because they love sincerity and righteousness. They are peaceful and sober, and they await the bridegroom. They are strangers to the whole world.
Contempt is far from them, and mockers are hateful in their eyes. The chambers of their hearts are filled with good treasures.
Their consciences are pure of deceit. The eyes of their minds are fixed on the heights, and they gaze at the beauty of their Lord and rejoice in him at all times.
Their heart conceives every good thing, and their lips bring forth good fruit. They have received good seed from their Lord / their Lord’s good seed.
They remove the evil thorns from it and throw them away. Their seed yields fruit a hundredfold, because they have watered it from the fountain of life.
Humility is planted within them and produces the fruits of faith and love. They have put on Christ like a fine garment,
and they keep it free from every impurity. The Spirit they have received dwells in them; they cherish the Spirit and do not cause the Spirit distress.
They adorn their temples for the great King, and he enters and dwells among the gentle and humble. Their buildings are set on the rock of truth,
and they are not afraid of waves and winds. Their deeds shine like lamps, and their light shines before them.
They prepare [?] for the bridegroom who is coming, and they wait to enter his bridal chamber. They receive money and trade with it, and they desire to gain ten talents.
They spend and distribute their possessions, and do not tie up money and hide it. Their visible body walks on the earth,
but all their thoughts are directed toward their Lord. They journey and walk along the narrow and constricted road, and they enter through the narrow gate of the kingdom.
They restrain their inclination in order to keep the law, on which they meditate at all times. They ponder it and conduct themselves in accordance with it, living in the world like strangers.
They await that city which is in heaven. Their mind is caught up and set on the heights, and they wait to enter the sanctuary there.
Their eyes are open and they gaze there, and they see the bridegroom preparing himself. Their messengers go there every day,
and carry and bring back peace and well-being. Their names are written in the book of life, and they pray and groan so that they may not be erased from it.
They bring their offerings—fasting and prayer—as a bribe to the one who has authority to write and to erase. They write their Lord’s law on their heart,
so that they may be written in that everlasting book. They wipe away their sins at all times, so that their names may not be wiped out of the book of life.
They love the afflictions of this present time, so that they may be kept far from everlasting torment. They teach their tongue / their tongues the songs of Christ,
so that they may delight in the place whose melodies are pleasant and sweet. They stretch out their hands to knock at that place, and they are needy so that need may be upon them.
These are the lovers of humility, those whose peace with everyone is great. The humble are children of the Exalted One,
and brothers of Christ, who, when he was announced, came to us with a greeting of peace. Because of his humility, Mary received him.
For when Gabriel brought the good news to blessed Mary, he said to her: “Peace to you, blessed among women.”
Gabriel carried and brought peace to the blessed fruit, and the beloved child was sown within Mary. She praised and magnified the Lord,
who delighted in the humility of his servant and did not delight in the haughty and proud. The Exalted One exalts all the humble. See, my beloved, how peace runs toward the humble.
And when the teacher of humility was born, the heavenly watchers praised him in these words: “Peace in heaven and glory on earth,
and good hope for humankind.” When he taught humility at his coming, he said: “If someone strikes you on your cheek, offer him the other one.”
If someone compels you to go a mile with him, go two more with him. If someone wants to take your tunic, give him your cloak too.
All these things, which our Savior also [?], the humble can do. Loftiness and pride do not suit the humble.
Nor does a crown suit the heads of the poor. A humble person who exalts himself is hated by his master, and a poor person who puts a crown on his head is killed by the king.
Pride and loftiness are the crown of our majestic King. For this reason, pride suits him alone, because it belongs to him
and is the emblem of his kingdom. Loftiness also suits his nature, but it is hateful and abhorrent in human beings. The standards and emblems of kingship
suit the king, not those of lower standing. Therefore, my beloved, let what God hates in us but loves in himself not be found among us.
Rather, let what belongs to him remain with him, and let us remain within our nature. Humility suits us, and loftiness and pride suit him. He has given us humility as our own.
Let us not take what he has not given us. Even if he does give it to us, he is testing us. For whoever takes something that is not his
is considered a wrongdoer and a liar. But whoever remains humble within his nature is exalted by the Most High. Do not pursue pride.
For a person cannot serve two masters. Loftiness has no fellowship with humility, nor arrogance with modesty.
Nor does insolence have fellowship with gentleness, nor impulsiveness with self-restraint. Whoever accepts loftiness here
is deprived of the world to come. Everyone who loves humility is raised up and exalted in the place of majesty.
The rich man who wore purple exalted himself, lifted himself up, and boasted. When he went there, he fell into torment.
But Lazarus, who humbled himself, was raised up and sat in Abraham’s bosom. A Pharisee and a tax collector were praying in the temple.
The Pharisee exalted himself and declared himself righteous, and he went down to his house without being acquitted. But the tax collector, who humbled himself, went down to his house justified.
Evil has been set against good, darkness against light, hostility against righteousness, and humility against envy,
and silence against strife. Evil has no power to stand against good, and when darkness sees the light, it flees.
Sweetness takes away bitterness, humility overcomes hostility, and righteousness puts an end to envy.
Silence extinguishes strife. For darkness does not envy gloom, nor is hostility jealous of violence.
Nor does envy mock strife, nor does bitterness hate [?]. Rather, the wicked are jealous of the good, and the ungodly envy the righteous.
The lofty boast over the humble, liars mock the truthful, and fools despise the wise.
Whoever has no truth in him does not want upright people to be found. To someone clothed in loftiness, a humble person looks like his murderer.
Someone whose hands are entangled in injustice takes no pleasure in a righteous person. To someone whose mouth is full of lies, truth is hateful and abhorrent.
There is no remedy for envy except silence and humility. An evil punishment comes upon envy. Because the serpent envied Adam in Paradise,
he received three curses as punishment: he took his feet away from him, and he crawled on his belly; he took away his food and gave him dust.
And he made him an enemy and gave him to mankind to trample underfoot. And Cain, who killed Abel out of envy, received curses for seven generations.
And he became a trembling wanderer on the earth. And Esau envied his brother Jacob and persecuted him, but humble Jacob received his birthright and his blessings.
And the proud one became subject to the humble one. As for those who envied humble Joseph, Joseph was exalted, and those who hated him fell down and bowed before him.
And Pharaoh, who envied the Hebrew people and commanded that their newborn children perish in the water, was judged by the very judgment he had pronounced and received punishment for his sins.
And Korah and his companions, who envied Moses, were overtaken by terrible punishment. Sheol opened its mouth and swallowed him, and fire blazed up and consumed him.
And when Aaron and Miriam envied humble Moses, the Holy One appeared to destroy them, and Miriam became leprous for seven days.
And Saul, who envied humble David and hated him, was abandoned by the Holy Spirit, and a tormenting spirit troubled him.
And Ahab, who envied Naboth and killed him—in the place where the dogs had licked Naboth’s blood, the dogs also licked his own blood.
And Jezebel, who persecuted Elijah, could do nothing to harm him. The dogs ate her, while Elijah went up to heaven.
And the accusers who envied the righteous men were themselves consumed by the fiery flame, while the upright men were rescued from it.
And the Chaldeans who accused Daniel filled with their own bodies the pit they had dug for him. And Haman, who envied Mordecai and his people,
did not succeed with his decree, and he and his sons suffered death on a cross. And the foolish people who did not accept the humble King Messiah—
he uprooted them from their land and scattered them. And when he receives the kingdom and returns, his enemies will be destroyed before him.

I have reminded you, my beloved, of all these things that I have written, and I have not grown weary of doing so, so that this saying may be firmly established for you: the wicked receive terrible punishment at the hands of the humble.
Therefore, my beloved, let this saying be firmly established for you: whoever clothes himself in envy has the Evil One dwelling within him, and the unclean spirit that dwelt in Saul dwells in him.
And while David was playing the harp for Saul to give him relief, Saul, in the envy with which he had clothed himself, threw a spear at his benefactor.
And whoever has humility within him has the Gentle and Humble One dwelling in him, and he becomes a dwelling place for Christ. Remember also what I wrote to you above:
the good do not envy the wicked, but the wicked envy the good. You have never seen a rich person envy the poor,
nor the righteous envy the wicked, nor the upright envy wrongdoers, nor peaceful people envy turmoil, nor the truthful envy liars.
Nor do the well-behaved envy the corrupt, nor the modest those who insult others. Therefore, pursue humility, which conquers envy
and puts an end to strife. Join silence and patience to it, so that you may be spared much strife. Love humility and acquire modesty,
and join patience to both of them. Many people love the humble, but even wrongdoers like themselves hate the proud. Hate anger,
and free yourself from hateful blemishes. Do not open your mouth to your anger, or let your face take on changing colors because of it, or reveal it to your tongue,
so that it does not produce evil fruit. Do not let the conceptions of anger be born in you, lest many minds conceive through their offspring.
When anger is conceived in you, it becomes an abscess. Do not give birth to it through your tongue or put it on your lips. All the thoughts that arise in your heart,
Hide them in your inner chamber. Give your tongue the good things your heart has conceived, and let your mouth learn beautiful words.
Let a word turn over in your heart for many days. Examine it: if it is fitting, give it to your tongue; if it is not fitting, let it die in your heart.
Bury it in your thoughts. Guard your tongue against false testimony, so that you do not bring fire upon your whole body. Let the King's Son who lives in you grow well.
Do not bring evil troubles in alongside him. For he wishes to dwell alone within a human being, and he does not dwell with someone whose thoughts are many.
Let your tongue love silence, because you lick your Lord's wounds. Let your lips guard against division,
because with them you kiss the King's Son. Let no idle talk come out of your mouth, lest he become disgusted with you and cease to live in you.
Love humility, a strong wall like iron. Love chastity, sweet fruit: whoever eats of it has a soul that is satisfied, happy, and glad.
All trees are tasted through their fruit, and a person's thoughts are tasted through their mouth.
A wise person tastes the mind of everyone who approaches by what their tongue says, because the lips speak from the heart's abundance.
Anyone who fears God always speaks good things, reciting and speaking of his Lord's law. Even when he hears words of frivolity,
he does not give them his attention. He speaks every kind of good word, and there are no harmful words in his mouth,
because his mind does not conceive anything hateful. This is how a person who meditates on his Lord's law is tasted.
These are the fruits of the good tree. As for a person who thinks evil things, a wise person tastes him through his lips.
If he speaks all kinds of frivolous, mocking, insulting, and blasphemous words, whoever hears him recognizes him. For these things are first conceived,
and then they are born, because in everything pregnancy leads to birth. Remember what our Savior said: a good tree produces good fruit,
and a bad tree produces bad fruit. A bad tree cannot produce good fruit, nor can a good tree produce bad fruit,
because a tree is known by its fruit. Likewise, a good person brings out and speaks good things from the good treasures in his heart,
and an evil person brings out and speaks evil things from the evil treasures in his heart, because the lips speak from the heart's abundance.
For even if a tree has a thousand fruits, you can taste the whole tree from one. And if you taste one of the fruits of a tree
whose fruits are many, good, and sweet, your soul longs for you alone to eat all the fruit of that tree.
So it is with a wise person: when he approaches an evil person, he first tastes him through his words. If he sees that his words are rotten,
he no longer wants to listen to them. If a wise person approaches someone wise and well instructed, he sits and stays beside him until he has tasted his words.
If he sees that they are good and sweet, full of knowledge and understanding, from that moment he wants to hear and learn all his words.
A wise person also discerns someone who is called humble by his taste / his words /. There is someone who appears innocent, quiet, and humble,
but whose heart thinks rotten things. That foolish humble person looks like one of the wise humble people who think good things.
To the azarole /bitter fruit/ mixed with quince: its appearance resembles quince, but its taste makes the palate bitter.
Love humility, my beloved, for its fragrance is pleasant and its taste is sweet. A humble person who remains humble even in an exalted position is loved by both the high and the low.

Even if humiliation befalls him, he is not disgraced, for he conducts himself according to the nature in which he already stood. But an exalted person who does not humble himself, when humiliation befalls him—
Great is his fall, because he did not humble himself in his exalted position. The humble person's friends are many, and those who greet him are beyond counting.
Many recount his praises, and his humility conceals his shortcomings, for in his heart he speaks no evil of anyone.

The humble person sits and meditates on wisdom, and his understanding reaches to the height of heaven. The humble person's words receive attention and are heard, for he shapes them and brings them out in due measure.
The chambers of his heart are full of good treasures, and his tongue produces pleasant fruit. Humility is a fountain of peace,
And streams of tranquility flow from it. Noah loved humility, and it sheltered him from the waters of the flood. Abraham drew near to it,
And became an heir in the land of the living. He fell down before God and humbled himself like dust and ashes. Isaac was brought up in it, in humility,
And kings became acquainted with him and welcomed a covenant with him. Jacob was a blameless man and lived in a tent, and he received Esau's blessings from his father.
Each one of our forefathers was humble, modest, and meek. The Most High raised up the humble and humbled the exalted,
And brought them down to disgrace. Job loved humility, and his Lord testified to his integrity. Wicked Satan envied him, and Job put him to shame—
The enemy who opposes the righteous. His Lord exalted Job because he persevered in his integrity, as his own mouth testified.
Love this portion, my beloved, the nature in which people of flesh dwell. This is righteousness: that a person should humble himself.
Adam's nature was of dust, for he came from the earth. His Lord gave him a commandment to keep, so that, when he kept what he had been commanded,
His Lord would bring him to an exalted nature. But because he wished to take for himself an exalted position that did not belong to his nature, his Lord returned him to his original, lowly nature.
Our Savior testified to this and said, “Everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and everyone who humbles himself will be exalted.” Adam exalted himself and was humbled,
And returned to dust, to his original nature. Our Savior, high and glorious, humbled himself, and was exalted and raised up to that original nature of his.
Glory was added to him, and everything was subjected to him. Our Savior, who humbled himself, received glory and received an increase. But Adam, who exalted himself,
Received humiliation and received curses in addition to humiliation. For this reason, my beloved, it is fitting and right for a person who loves God
To love humility and remain in his humble nature, with his root planted in the earth and his fruits rising before the Lord of majesty.
Humility, whose fruits are desirable: meekness, modesty, and pleasant thoughts are found with it.
The humble are sincere and patient, beloved, blameless, and righteous, skillful in doing good, discerning, quiet, and wise,
Gentle, peaceable, merciful, repentant, compassionate, profound, measured, beautiful, and desirable.
Whoever loves this tree, whose fruits are these—blessed is his soul, for it dwells at rest, and he who delights in the peaceful and the humble dwells within him.
The Demonstration on Humility is finished.
The Demonstration on Shepherds
The shepherds sit at the head of the flock and give the sheep life-giving food. Whoever keeps watch and labors for his sheep
cares for his flock and is a disciple of the good shepherd, who gave his life for his sheep. But whoever does not tend his flock well
resembles the hired worker, who does not care about the sheep. Shepherds, imitate those righteous shepherds of old.
Jacob tended Laban’s sheep, guarded them, labored, kept watch, and received his wages. For Jacob said to Laban, “Look, I have been with you for twenty years.
I did not shear your sheep or your flocks, and I did not eat the rams of your flock. I did not bring you an animal torn by beasts, for you demanded compensation from me.
By day the heat consumed me, and by night the frost, and sleep fled from my eyes.” Shepherds, look at this shepherd and how much he cared for his flock!
He stayed awake at night to guard them, and by day he kept watch and labored to pasture them. Jacob was a shepherd, Joseph was a shepherd, and his brothers were shepherds.
Moses was a shepherd, David too was a shepherd, and Amos was a shepherd. All these were shepherds who tended sheep and led them well.
But why, my beloved, did these shepherds first tend sheep and then get chosen to shepherd human beings?
It was so that they would learn how a shepherd cares for his sheep and keeps watch and labors for them. Once they had learned the ways of shepherds,
they were chosen for leadership. Jacob tended Laban’s sheep, labored, kept watch, and led them well. Then he shepherded his sons and led them well,
and taught them the pattern of shepherding. Joseph tended sheep with his brothers, and in Egypt he became the leader of a great people.
He cared for them as a good shepherd cares for his flock. Moses tended the sheep of his father-in-law Jethro, and he was chosen from among the sheep to shepherd his people.
He led them like a good shepherd. Moses carried his staff on his shoulder and walked at the head of the people he was leading.
He shepherded them for forty years and kept watch and labored for his sheep. As a diligent and good shepherd, when his Lord wanted to wipe them out
because of their sins in worshiping the calf, Moses prayed and pleaded with his Lord, saying, “Either forgive the people their sins,
or else erase me from the book you have written.” This is the faithful shepherd who surrendered his life for his sheep. He is the excellent leader
who gave his life for his sheep. He is the compassionate father who cherished his children and raised them. Moses trained a great and wise [?],
who knew how to care for a flock: Joshua son of Nun, a man of the Spirit, who led the flock, the entire camp of Israel. He destroyed kings and conquered the land.
He gave them land for pasture and allotted resting places of the folds / and a fold / for his sheep. David too tended his father’s sheep,
and he was taken from among the sheep to shepherd his people. He shepherded them with integrity of heart and led them with skillful hands.
When David counted his flock of sheep, wrath rose against them, and they began to be destroyed. Then David surrendered himself for his sheep,
praying and saying, “Lord God, I sinned by counting Israel. Let your hand fall on me and on my father’s household.”
What sin have these innocent sheep committed? All diligent shepherds likewise used to give their lives for their sheep.
But those shepherds who did not care about the sheep are hired workers who tended only themselves.
For this reason the prophet called out to them and said, “O shepherds who destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture, hear the word of the Lord!”
This is what the Lord says: “Look, I myself will attend to my sheep, as a shepherd attends to his flock on a stormy day, and I will demand my sheep from your hands.
You foolish shepherds! You wear the sheep’s wool and eat the flesh of the fat ones, but you do not tend the sheep.
You have not healed the sick, bandaged the injured, strengthened the weak, or gathered the lost and scattered.
You have not protected the strong and fat ones, but have subjected them to force. You graze in good pasture,
but you trample what remains with your feet. You drink sweet water, but you muddy what remains with your feet.
My sheep grazed on what your feet had trampled and drank the water your feet had muddied.” These are the greedy, worthless shepherds and hired workers
who did not tend the sheep and lead them well, and did not rescue them from wolves. But when the great shepherd comes, the chief shepherd calls and attends to his sheep,
inspects his flock, brings those shepherds forward, settles accounts with them, and condemns them for their deeds.
But those who tended the sheep well, the chief shepherd makes glad and grants them life and rest as their inheritance. “O ignorant and foolish shepherd,
you who have abandoned my sheep! Against your right hand and against your right eye [?], because you said about the flock, ‘Let the dying die, and let the lost perish.
Let whichever one remains eat the flesh of its companions.’ Therefore, look, I will blind your right eye and wither your right arm.
Your eye that looked for a bribe will go blind, and your hand that did not guide justly will become useless. But you,” he says, “my sheep, the sheep of my pasture,
are human beings, and I am the Lord your God. Look, from now on I will pasture you in good, rich pasture.”
The good shepherd gives his life for his sheep. And again he said, “I have other sheep, and I must bring them here too.
All the sheep will become one flock, with one shepherd. My Father loves me for this reason: because I give my life for the sheep.” And again he said,
“I am the gate for the sheep. Everyone who enters through me will live, and will go in and out and find pasture.” You shepherds, imitate this diligent shepherd,
the head of the entire flock. How greatly he cared for his flock! He brought near those far away, brought back the strays, and attended to the sick.
He strengthened the weak, bandaged the injured, and protected the fat ones. He gave up his life for the sheep, and chose and taught outstanding [?].
He entrusted the sheep to their hands and gave them authority over his entire flock. For he said to Simon Peter,
“Tend my sheep, my lambs, and my ewes for me.” Simon tended his sheep, and his time came to an end. He entrusted the flock to you and departed.
You too must tend them and lead them well. For a shepherd who cares about his sheep does no other work alongside this. He does not establish a vineyard,
nor does he plant gardens or become entangled in the troubles of this world. We have never seen a shepherd leave his sheep in the wilderness and become a merchant.
Nor should he neglect his flock and become a farmer. But if he leaves his flock and cultivates these things, he has handed his flock over to wolves.
Remember, my dear friend, what I wrote to you about our forefathers: they first learned the ways of sheep, and from this gained experience in caring for them.
Then they were chosen for leadership, so that they might learn and see how much a shepherd cares for his flock.
Just as they guided the sheep with care, so they were to become accomplished in this leadership as well. For Joseph was chosen from among the sheep
to lead the Egyptians in a time of distress. Moses too was chosen from among the sheep to lead his people and shepherd them.
David was taken from following the sheep to become king over Israel. And Amos's Lord took him from following the sheep and made him a prophet over his people.
Elisha too was taken from behind the plow to become a prophet in Israel. Moses did not return to his sheep or abandon the flock entrusted to him.
David did not return to his father's sheep, but led his people with integrity of heart. Amos did not return to tending sheep and gathering wood,
but carried out and completed his prophetic ministry. Elisha did not return to his plow, but served Elijah and took his place. As for the attendant he had,
because he loved villages, commerce, vineyards, olive trees, and farming, Elisha was unwilling to have him as a disciple and did not entrust the flock to him.
I ask you, shepherds, not to appoint foolish and ignorant attendants over the flock, nor greedy people or lovers of possessions.
Let everyone who tends sheep eat of their milk, and let whoever guides a plow benefit from his labor. It is fitting for priests to receive a share from the altar,
and let the Levites receive their tithes. Let whoever eats of the milk set his heart on his flock, and let whoever benefits from the labor of his plow
be diligent in his work. Let the priests who receive a share from the altar serve the altar in purity. And the Levites who receive tithes
have no allotted inheritance in Israel. You shepherds, disciples of our great Shepherd, do not be like hired workers,
because a hired worker does not care about the sheep. Instead, imitate our kind Shepherd, who did not hold his own life dearer than his sheep. Raise the young men and honor the virgins,
and love the lambs, and let them grow up in your arms, so that when you go to the Chief Shepherd, you may present your entire flock to him intact.
Then he will give you what he promised: “Where I am, you too will be.” These few words are sufficient for shepherds and good attendants.
Earlier, my dear friend, I wrote to remind you of the conduct appropriate to the whole flock. In this discourse I have written to you
about the shepherds who lead the flock. I have written these reminders to you, my dear friend, in response to what you asked me in your dear letter.
The steward brought me into the king's treasury and showed me many good things there. When I saw them, my mind was captivated by the great treasure.
As I gazed at it, it dazzled the eyes, captivated the thoughts, and astonished the mind with its many colors. Whoever takes from it becomes rich and enriches others.
It stands open and accessible to all who seek it. Though many take from it, it loses nothing. And when they give from what they have received,
their own portion increases greatly. Let those who receive freely give freely, just as they received. For it cannot be bought for money, because nothing is equal to it.
For neither is the treasure depleted nor are those who take from it satisfied. They drink and long for more; they eat and remain hungry. Whoever is not thirsty cannot drink.
And whoever is not hungry cannot eat. His hunger satisfies many, and from his thirst springs flow.
For a person who approaches the fear of God is like a thirsty man who approaches a spring, drinks, and is satisfied, while the spring loses nothing.
And land that needs water to drink drinks from the spring, yet its waters do not run out. And after the land drinks, it still needs to drink again.
And the spring is not diminished by its flowing. So it is with the knowledge of God: even if all human beings take from it,
it suffers no loss at all. Nor can mortals encompass it. Whoever takes from it never finishes taking, and when it gives, it loses nothing.
When you take fire from a blaze with a lamp, you light many lamps from it. The blaze loses nothing when you take from it,
nor is the lamp diminished when it lights many others. No single person can take the king’s entire treasury. Nor, when a thirsty person drinks from a spring,
do its waters run out. And [?] when someone stands on a high mountain, his eye takes in what is near and far.
Nor, even if he stands counting the stars of heaven, can he encompass the heavenly hosts. Nor, when he approaches the fear of God,
can he take it all. Even if he takes a very great deal, no diminution of it is apparent. Nor, when he gives some of what he has taken,
does it run out for him, or does he reach its limit. And remember, my dear friend, what I wrote to you in the first discourse, on faith: whoever receives freely
ought to give freely, just as he received. As our Lord said, “You received freely; give freely.” For whoever holds back some of what he has received,
even what he received will be taken away from him. Therefore, my dear friend, as much as I was able to take at this time from that inexhaustible treasury,
I have sent you from it. And although I have sent it to you, it is all still with me. For the treasury suffers no loss, since it is the wisdom of God.
And its steward is our Lord Jesus Christ, as he himself testified, saying, “Everything has been handed over to me by my Father.” And although he is the steward of wisdom,
he himself is also wisdom, as the apostle said: “Christ is the power of God and his wisdom.” This wisdom has been distributed to many,
yet it loses nothing, as I explained to you above: the prophets received from the Spirit of Christ, and Christ was not diminished at all.
I have written ten discourses for you, my dear friend, on what you asked me. I have explained to you [?], and I have given you what you did not ask of me.
I asked your name and wrote to you, and I asked myself your question. And I answered you according to what I was able to explain to you. These things that I have written to you—
meditate on them at all times, and work diligently at reading the Scriptures that are read in the church of God. These ten books of [?]
that I have written to you draw upon one another and are built upon one another. Do not separate them from one another. I have written to you from Aleph to Yod,
one letter after another. Read and learn, you and the brothers who are members of the covenant and share our faith, who keep far from mockery,
as I wrote to you above. And remember what I set down for you: I have not brought these words to their full conclusion, but have stopped short of it.
Nor are these enough. But hear these things from me without contention, and investigate them with our brothers who are willing to be persuaded.
Accept everything you hear that builds up the building, and tear down everything that builds up other teachings.
and tears down its ruins, because he cannot build another. But I, my dear friend, have brought stones for the building like a stonecutter.
Let skilled architects carve them and place them in the building. All the workers who labor on the building receive their wages from the master of the house.
The Demonstration on Shepherds is complete.
Demonstration on Circumcision
When God blessed Abraham and made him head of all the faithful, righteous, and upright, God did not appoint him as father of just one people,
but of many nations, when he said to him, “Your name shall no longer be called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, because I have appointed you father of a multitude of nations.”
Now, my dear and beloved friend, listen to the purpose of this discourse and the foundation of the argument that ought to be made against the people who stand before us,
who think of themselves as Abraham’s offspring, but do not understand that they have been called rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah,
and that their father was an Amorite and their mother a Hittite, and that they are rejected silver and rebellious children. Moses their leader testified against them and said to them,
“You have been rebellious from the day I knew you.” Again, he repeated in the song of testimony, “Your vine comes from the vine of Sodom and from the planting of Gomorrah.
Your grapes are bitter grapes, and your clusters are bitterness to you.” In that hymn of testimony he also pointed to the people from among the nations,
when he said to them, “I will make you jealous through a people who are not a people, and through a foolish people I will provoke you to anger.” And the Holy One testified through Isaiah,
when he said, “I planted a vineyard and cultivated it, but instead of grapes it produced carobs.” Jeremiah the prophet also spoke
about the congregation of the people: “I planted you as a vine shoot, entirely of true stock, but you changed and rebelled against me like a foreign vine.”
And Ezekiel testified about the vine that fire had consumed its branches and its middle was scorched, and that it was no longer fit for any work.
It had been planted as a vine shoot of true stock—their early ancestors—but the children turned to the unclean deeds of the Amorites.
For people from every nation, when they practice righteousness, are called children and heirs of Abraham their father.
But Abraham’s children, when they practice the unclean deeds of foreign nations, become Sodomites and the people of Gomorrah,
as Isaiah testified against them, saying, “Hear the word of the Lord, rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah.” Otherwise, tell me, wise man:
what rulers and people were there in Sodom and Gomorrah in the days of Isaiah the prophet? For those cities had been overthrown in wrath since the days of Lot,
and they will never be inhabited again. Ezekiel also reveals Sodom’s wickedness and calls her Jerusalem’s sister, when he says to her,
“Your sister Sodom and her daughters did not do evil deeds like those you and your daughters have done. This was the wickedness of Sodom and her daughters:
she did not support the afflicted and the poor. When I saw these deeds among them, I overthrew them.” Since Sodom and Gomorrah, their companions, had been overthrown long before,

why did Isaiah say, “Listen, rulers of Sodom and people of Gomorrah,” unless it was so that they would understand that he was calling them this because they practiced and engaged in the deeds of the Sodomites?
For they are circumcised yet uncircumcised, and they were chosen but have been rejected. They boast, saying, “We are circumcised and chosen and distinguished from all the nations.”
For this is known to everyone who understands: circumcision without faith has no use or benefit.
For faith came before circumcision, and circumcision was given to Abraham as a sign and a covenant, as God said to him:
“This is my covenant, which you shall keep: you shall circumcise every male.” And during the time that pleased its giver, it was observed along with the commandments of the law.
It benefited people and gave life. But when the law was not observed, circumcision did no good. Jeroboam son of Nebat, one of the descendants of Joseph,
from the tribe of Ephraim, was circumcised as the Holy One had commanded Abraham and as Moses had instructed in the law.
And all the kings of Israel who followed the law of Jeroboam were circumcised and set apart, yet no good remembrance of them was recorded,
because of their sins. What benefit did Jeroboam gain from his circumcision, or all the kings of Israel who followed in his footsteps?
Or what use and benefit did Manasseh son of Hezekiah gain, whose sins were so numerous that God could no longer forgive Jerusalem?
Throughout all generations and ages, God gave his covenants, generation by generation, as he pleased. They were observed in their own times and were replaced.
For he commanded Adam not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. And because he did not keep the commandment and the covenant, he was condemned.
And Enoch, who pleased God—it was not because he had kept the commandment concerning the tree that God transferred him to life, but because he believed.
And good conduct is not the same as the commandment not to eat from the tree. And Noah, who maintained integrity and righteousness, God rescued from the wrath of the flood.

And he established a covenant with him and with his descendants after him—after him—that they should increase and multiply, and the covenant of the rainbow in the clouds between God and the earth and all flesh.
Circumcision was not given with any one of those covenants. And when he chose Abraham, it was not through circumcision that he called and chose him
and appointed him to be the father of all nations, but through faith. Only after he believed did he command him to be circumcised.
For if life came through circumcision, Abraham would first have been circumcised and then would have believed.
And if circumcision had been given for gaining eternal life, Scripture would have declared, “Abraham was circumcised, and his circumcision was credited to him as righteousness.”
But this is what is written: “Abraham believed God, and his faith was credited to him as righteousness.” For those who believed while uncircumcised received life.
And those who were circumcised but did not believe gained nothing from their circumcision. Abel, Enoch, Noah, Shem, and Japheth did not please God through circumcision,
but because each of them kept their covenants in their own times and believed that there is one who gives covenants in every generation as he wills.
Melchizedek was a priest of God Most High. He blessed Abraham while he was uncircumcised, and it is well known that the lesser is blessed by the greater.
Now, my beloved, listen, and I will show you for what purpose circumcision was given. For when Abraham believed and left Ur of the Chaldeans and came to live in Haran,
God did not command him to be circumcised. And while he lived in the land of Canaan for twenty-four years, he was not circumcised, because he had no son who was the son of the promise,
from whom righteous people, kings, priests, and anointed ones would be born. But when he was ninety-nine years old,
the Holy One made known to him that when he reached a hundred years, a son would be born to him. Then he circumcised him, for when he was a hundred years old, Isaac was born to him.

And he commanded him to circumcise the flesh of his foreskin, as a mark and sign of the covenant, so that when his descendants multiplied, they would be distinct from all the nations among whom they lived.
This was so that they would not become involved in their unclean deeds. And Abraham circumcised the flesh of his foreskin when he was ninety-nine years old.
He also circumcised his son Ishmael, who was thirteen years old. Abraham circumcised those born in his household and those bought with his money that very day,
as God had told him. After he was circumcised, Isaac was conceived and born, and he was circumcised on the eighth day. Circumcision was observed among Abraham’s descendants,
by Isaac and Ishmael, by Jacob and his sons, and by Esau and his descendants, for one hundred and ninety years, until Jacob entered Egypt.
In Egypt, Jacob’s descendants observed it for two hundred and twenty-five years, until they went out into the wilderness. And when Lot saw that his uncle Abraham had been circumcised,
he too circumcised his descendants after he had separated from him. They maintained circumcision as a custom, although they did not believe.
But if life comes through circumcision, then the descendants of Ishmael, the descendants of Keturah, the descendants of Lot, and the descendants of Esau
also have life, for they are circumcised. Yet although they are circumcised, they worship many idols. But Jeremiah the prophet showed me plainly
that all the circumcised who do not believe are uncircumcised, and that their circumcision does not deliver them from wrath.
For he said, “Look, I will punish everyone who is circumcised in uncircumcision: the Egyptians and the Jews, Moab and Edom, and the Ammonites,
and all those who clip the edges of their hair and live in the wilderness. For all the nations are uncircumcised, and all the house of Israel are uncircumcised in their hearts.”
If they benefited from circumcision, why is the Jew counted with the Egyptians, the Edomites, the Moabites,
the Ammonites, and those who clip the edges of their hair, who are the descendants of Hagar and the descendants of Keturah? Clearly, however, their circumcision became uncircumcision.
For wrath also brought punishment upon Judah, just as upon all these who are circumcised in uncircumcision. For when the Holy One saw that they were saying,
“We have life because we are Abraham’s descendants and are circumcised,” while they would not bend their stiff necks in submission to the law,
he said to them through the prophet, “Circumcise the foreskin of your hearts, and no longer stiffen your necks.” It is clear that for anyone who has not circumcised the foreskin of his heart,
circumcision of the flesh is of no benefit either, just as it did not benefit anyone who was circumcised in uncircumcision.
And to establish for you, my beloved, that circumcision is a mark intended to distinguish them from the unclean nations,
consider that when he brought them out of Egypt and they traveled in the wilderness for forty years, they did not circumcise, because they were one people
and were not mingling with other nations. There he did not mark them, because they were grazing by themselves.
In marking Abraham’s descendants, it was not because all the nations did not belong to him that he set Abraham’s descendants apart as a portion for himself.
Rather, he abandoned all the nations that practiced the evil deeds of paganism because of their deeds. And his marking of his people
was not to make known to himself that they were Abraham’s descendants, because even without marking them, he knew them.
Rather, it was so that they would recognize one another and not hide behind false excuses. For such a thing could have happened if they had not been marked.
So that when some of them were found worshiping idols, or committing sexual immorality or adultery, or stealing, or doing anything contrary to the law,
those among them who were caught doing these things would deny it and disclaim being descendants of Abraham, so that they would not be killed and receive punishment
and the death sentence prescribed in the law for those who engage in these things. But anyone found to have broken the law
and to be engaging in one of these hateful practices can no longer hide behind the false excuse, “I am not one of Abraham’s offspring and descendants.”
For if he is found to have denied it, they identify him by his circumcision and punish him as his offense deserves.
For if circumcision had not been given for this purpose, they would have been required to be circumcised in the wilderness too. But because they were separated from the nations
and were roaming by themselves in the wilderness, they were not marked. And when they were crossing the Jordan, the Lord commanded Joshua son of Nun and said to him,
“Circumcise the Israelites again, a second time.” And why did he tell Joshua to circumcise them a second time?
It was because they were circumcised in their hearts, as he said through the prophet: “Circumcise the foreskin of your hearts, and no longer stiffen your necks.”
Joshua then circumcised them again and marked them in their flesh a second time. Otherwise, how do you understand the statement
that Joshua circumcised the people a second time? For they had not been circumcised in their flesh, because after Joshua circumcised them, Scripture testified
that these were the ones Joshua circumcised: all who had been born in the wilderness, because none of the children born in the wilderness had been circumcised.

Now look, my dear friend, and marvel at this: the circumcised people who came out of Egypt died in the wilderness because of their sins, because they provoked the spirit of the Holy One and did not believe him.
It is clear that if they had believed, they would not have been prevented from entering the promised land. And Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh
survived out of the six hundred thousand who came out of Egypt, and they entered the land and took possession of it. And the children in the wilderness who believed, though uncircumcised, lived
and entered to take possession of the land. He circumcised them as they were entering the land of the Canaanites, and two circumcisions were credited to them.
And why, when he brings wrath upon all who are circumcised in the foreskin, did he also include the Egyptians, who were not Abraham’s offspring,
like the Moabites and Ammonites, who are descendants of Lot, Abraham’s nephew, and like the Edomites, who are descendants of Esau,
and like those with clipped temples who live in the wilderness, who are descendants of Ishmael and descendants of Keturah, and Judah, the offspring of Jacob?
All these are offspring of Abraham’s household. The Egyptians adopted circumcision as a custom, without believing, from the Israelites while they were living among them.
They also adopted it from Joseph, for when Manasseh and Ephraim were born to him and he circumcised them, they too learned from Joseph and began to circumcise.
For Joseph’s command was carried out in everything throughout Egypt. And because there are some people, my dear friend, who say that when Pharaoh’s daughter found Moses,
she recognized from the covenant in his flesh that he was one of the Israelites—this is not how it was, as the account of the event makes clear.
For the covenant of Moses’ circumcision was no different at all from the circumcision of the Egyptians.
Anyone who does not know that the Egyptians are circumcised should be convinced by Jeremiah. For when Pharaoh’s daughter found Moses,
When she saw him floating in the river, she knew that he was one of the Hebrew children, because no order had been given for Egyptian children to be thrown into the river.
Pharaoh had given this order concerning the Israelites, saying that every male child born was to be thrown into the river. She knew that this had been done out of fear of the command.
When she saw that he had been placed in a wooden chest, she knew that his family had made him a chest because they could not hide him,
and had thrown him into the river. For if the Israelites had been distinguished by circumcision, while the Egyptians were uncircumcised,
Moses could not have been brought up in Pharaoh’s household, because during his childhood the covenant in his flesh would have been recognizable at all times.
And since Pharaoh’s daughter was breaking her father’s law and command, Pharaoh’s command and law were no longer being upheld anywhere in Egypt either.
I will also explain to you, my dear friend, about Keturah’s descendants: they too share a border with Ishmael’s descendants.
For when the Midianites, who are Keturah’s descendants, and the people of the east, who are Ishmael’s descendants, gathered together
and came to fight against Israel in the days of Gideon son of Joash, they sought jointly to subjugate Israel, but they were delivered into Gideon’s hands
with three hundred men. I have explained this to you about Keturah’s descendants because they and Ishmael’s descendants lived in the wilderness.
For from the time Abraham sent Hagar and Ishmael away, Ishmael and his offspring lived in the wilderness. This is what is written:
He lived in the wilderness and learned archery, so that his hand would be against everyone and everyone’s hand against him; and he settled along the border of all his brothers.
On one side of him, to the east, settled Esau’s descendants, who are the Edomites. For when Israel came out of Egypt,
they went around the land of Edom, the hill country of Esau. The Ammonites and Moabites also border them on the north,
and Keturah’s descendants share a border to the east with the Edomites, Esau’s descendants. For when Abraham sent Keturah’s descendants away,
he originally sent them eastward. Hagar’s descendants occupied the whole land of [?], and the Edomites, Esau’s descendants,
settled east of them all, as far as Bozrah. For although the Lord commanded Moses, “Do not approach the land of Esau’s descendants,
because I am not giving you any of their land, not even enough for the sole of a foot to tread on, because I have given the hill country of Seir to Esau.
Instead, buy food from them with money and eat, and buy water from them with money and drink,” Moses did as the Lord commanded him
and did not harass Esau’s descendants. But when he reached Rekem, he sent messengers with peaceful words to the king of Edom, saying to him,
“This is what your brother Jacob says: You know all the hardship that has overtaken us on the journey, and how the Egyptians enslaved us.
Now we are in Rekem, a town at the edge of your territory. Let us now pass through your land. We will travel along the King’s Highway.
Sell us food to eat, and we will also pay for the water that we and our livestock drink.” But he said to Israel, “You shall not pass through my territory,
or I will come out against you with the sword.” Israel turned away from them when he saw that they would not be persuaded. And as they passed along their border,
the Israelites took Bezer in the wilderness from them and took possession of it. They made it a city of refuge. And whoever wishes to accept the explanation,
To learn that Bozrah belonged to the descendants of Esau, who were the Edomites of old, let us hear from the prophet Isaiah, when he saw the Holy One coming from Edom,
with his garments red from Bozrah, because he had trampled them and crushed them, and exacted vengeance on the descendants of Esau,
because he did not welcome his brother and kept his anger forever. And anyone still not convinced that Bozrah served the Edomites long ago,
let him also hear from Genesis: when kings reigned in Edom, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah became king. And Isaiah also said,
“Look, it will descend upon the Edomites, upon the people condemned in judgment.” And David said, “Upon Edom I will cast my sandals,”
because Esau destroyed his compassion forever and kept his anger forever, and did not allow his brother to pass through his territory.
For this reason he was condemned in judgment, because he kept his resentment forever. And when Israel turned aside from his brother Esau, he sent messengers to the Moabites, the descendants of Lot,
so that they might pass through their territory. But they would not listen or agree. Instead, they hired Balaam son of Beor to curse them.
And because they did not allow them to pass peacefully through their territory, the Holy One commanded that no Ammonite or Moabite should enter the assembly of the Lord,
not even to the tenth generation, because they did not offer Israel bread and water on the road, but met them with the sword,

while Israel was exhausted and weary. But concerning the Egyptians and Edomites, he commanded Israel not to reject them: the Egyptians, because he had lived in their land, and the Edomite, because he was his brother.
I have explained and shown you all this so that you may know that Ishmael settled along the borders of all his brothers and became a wild donkey of a man.
Abraham gave gifts to the sons of Keturah and sent them away to their brother Ishmael, so that they would not be heirs with Isaac, the son of the promise.
For if life comes through circumcision, then the descendants of Ishmael, the descendants of Keturah, and the descendants of Lot—the Moabites and Ammonites—
and the descendants of Esau, the Edomites, and the Egyptians could boast even more. For they too are circumcised, yet they worship many idols.
It is therefore clear that circumcision is of no benefit without faith. But everyone who circumcises the foreskin of his heart believes and lives,
and becomes a son of Abraham. And the word that God spoke to Abraham is fulfilled: “I have made you the father of many nations.”
For the law and the covenant have been changed in every respect. Long ago God changed Adam’s covenant and gave another to Noah.
He also gave one to Abraham, and he changed Abraham’s and gave another to Moses. And when Moses’ covenant was not kept,
he gave another in the last age, a covenant that will not be changed. To Adam he gave a covenant that he should not eat from the tree; to Noah, the rainbow in the clouds.
As for Abraham, he first chose him because of his faith, and afterward gave circumcision as a seal and a mark for his descendants.
And Moses’ covenant was the lamb, so that he would pass over the people. All these covenants differ from one another. For the circumcision desired by the giver of the covenants
is the one Jeremiah spoke of: “Circumcise the foreskin of your hearts.” For if the covenant God gave Abraham is firm, this one too is firm and trustworthy.
And the lawgiver cannot be overruled by those who are outside the law or by those who are under the law.
For he gave Moses the law with its observances and covenants. And when they did not keep the law, he abolished its covenants and promised to give a new covenant.
And he said, “Not like the first,” although the giver of both is one and the same. For this is the covenant he promised to give: “They will all know me,
from their youngest to their oldest.” In this covenant there is no circumcision of the flesh or distinguishing mark of the people.
We know truly, my beloved, that in each generation God established laws. They served for as long as he pleased and were changed, as the apostle said:
“Formerly, in every form, the kingdom of God dwelt at all times.” This is known and clear to the wise and to anyone who understands:
that anyone who belongs to the covenant and lets himself be drawn after circumcision is circumcised because of his impurity and recklessness. He does not understand what the apostle said:
“I wish those who trouble you would even castrate themselves!” For our God is true, and his covenants are utterly trustworthy.
Every covenant was valid and trustworthy in its own time. Those circumcised in their hearts live and are circumcised a second time at the true Jordan: baptism for the forgiveness of sins.
Joshua son of Nun circumcised the people a second time with a flint blade, when he and his people crossed the Jordan. And Jesus our Savior circumcised the nations who believed in him a second time,
with circumcision of the heart. They were baptized, and they are circumcised with the blade that is his word, which is sharper than a two-edged sword.
Joshua son of Nun brought the people into the promised land. And Jesus our Savior promised the land of the living to everyone who crosses the true Jordan,
believes, and cuts away the foreskin of his heart. Joshua son of Nun set up stones as a witness in Israel. And Jesus our Savior called Simon a true rock,
and established him as a faithful witness among the nations. Joshua son of Nun celebrated the Passover on the plain of Jericho, in the accursed land,
and the people ate bread from the land. And Jesus our Savior celebrated the Passover with his disciples in the city of Jerusalem,

which he cursed, declaring that not one stone would be left upon another in it. There he gave the mystery in the bread of life. Joshua son of Nun condemned the greedy Achan, who stole and hid what he stole.
And Jesus our Savior condemned the greedy Judas, who stole and hid money from the money box he kept.
Joshua son of Nun destroyed the unclean nations. And Jesus our Savior overthrew Satan and his army. Joshua son of Nun made the sun stand still in the sky.
And Jesus our Savior made the sun set at noon when they crucified him. Joshua son of Nun was the savior of the people. And Jesus was called the Savior of the nations.
Blessed are those whose hearts are circumcised, freed from uncircumcision, and who are born of water in a second circumcision, becoming heirs with Abraham,
the faithful leader and father of all nations, whose faith was counted to him as righteousness.
The Demonstration on Circumcision is finished.
Demonstration on the Passover
The Holy One commanded Moses concerning the Passover, that he should celebrate it on the fourteenth day of the first month. For he said to Moses:
“Command the congregation of the Israelites to take for themselves one year-old lamb, a lamb without blemish. They shall take it from the lambs or the young goats,
and all the Israelites shall celebrate the Passover to the Lord.” For he told Moses that they should take a lamb on the tenth day of the month,
and keep it until the fourteenth day of that month. They should slaughter it at sunset and sprinkle some of its blood on the doorway of their houses to keep out the destroyer.
so that he would not enter their homes while the destroyer was at work in the land of Egypt. The whole congregation was to eat the lamb in haste.
And this, he said, is how they were to eat it: with their belts fastened around their waists, their sandals on their feet, and their staffs in their hands.
He instructed them to eat it in haste. They were not, he said, to eat any of it raw, nor boiled in water,
but roasted over fire. They were not to take any of it outside the house, nor break a bone in it. And the Israelites did so.
And Israel ate the Passover on the fourteenth day of the first month, which is Nisan, the month of blossoms, the first month, the month that begins the year.
Now consider, my dear friend, these mysteries that the Holy One commanded for observing the Passover. He instructed them about all its regulations and told them:
“It must be eaten in one house, and you must not take any of it outside the house.” And Moses commanded them as follows:

“When you enter the land that the Lord gives you and observe the Passover at its appointed time, you are not permitted to slaughter the Passover sacrifice in any of your towns, but only in the place that the Lord your God chooses for himself,
you and your household. And rejoice at your festival.” He also commanded them as follows: “A temporary resident or a hired worker must not eat any of the Passover.
But any slave you own who was bought with money may eat the Passover once the flesh of his foreskin has been circumcised.”
These mysteries are great and wonderful, my dear friend. If, when Israel was in its own land, it was not permitted to observe the Passover
except in Jerusalem alone, today, when it is scattered among all nations and languages, among the unclean and the uncircumcised,
and they eat their bread in uncleanness among the nations, as Ezekiel said about them—when he showed him a sign that he was to eat his bread in uncleanness, he pleaded and said:
“O Lord of lords, I have never been defiled, and no unclean meat has entered my mouth.” And he said to Ezekiel, “This will be a sign:
the Israelites will eat their bread like this, in uncleanness, among the nations where I will scatter them.” For if, as I said above,
when Israel was in its own land, it was not permitted to slaughter the Passover sacrifice anywhere it wished, but only before one altar in Jerusalem,
how can it observe the mystery of the Passover today, seeing that it is scattered among foreign nations? They no longer have authority to do so.
And through the prophet he testified about them as follows: “The Israelites will remain for many days without sacrifices and without an altar,
and without anyone wearing an ephod or offering incense.” Again, he said concerning Jerusalem, “I will put an end to her celebrations and her festivals, her new moons and her Sabbath / her Sabbaths.”
And concerning the ark of the covenant he said, “They will no longer say, ‘The ark of the covenant of the Lord.’ They will not remember it, and it will not be made again.”
Since he said that they would not remember it, that it would not be made, and that it would not come to mind, why do they dare to make it? And Moses had already said about them:
“I will make them jealous through a people that is no people, and through a foolish nation I will make them angry.” Now I ask you, wise interpreter of the people,
who do not examine the words of the Law: show me when this was fulfilled—that God made his people jealous through a people that is no people. And when did he make them angry through a foolish nation?
But if you are jealous of the people drawn from the nations, you are fulfilling the written word that Moses set down beforehand for you in the book.
And if you observe the Passover in various places where you live as a foreigner, you observe it in violation of the commandment, because a certificate of divorce has been written for you.
And if you are not convinced, listen to the prophet Jeremiah, who says, “I have abandoned my house; I have abandoned my inheritance.”
“I have handed the one my soul loves over to her enemies, and my inheritance has become to me a speckled bird.” What is this speckled bird?
I ask you. For the speckled bird is the church of the nations. See how he calls her speckled,
because she is gathered from many languages and brought near from distant nations. But if you are not convinced
that the nations have become God’s inheritance, listen again to what Jeremiah says when he calls the nations and rejects Israel.
For he says, “Stand at the roads and look, and ask about the ancient paths. See which road is good, and walk in it.”
“But you said, ‘We will not walk in it.’” And again he says, “I appointed watchmen over you so that you would listen to the sound of the trumpet.”
“But they said, ‘We will not listen.’” Then, when the children of Israel did not listen to him, he turned to the church from among the nations.
For he says, “Listen, nations, and understand, church among them.” And David says, “Remember your congregation, which you acquired long ago.”
And Isaiah says, “Listen, nations, to what I have done, and know my might, you who are far away.” And again Isaiah speaks about the church that was to come into being among the nations.
For he says, “In the last days, the mountain of the Lord’s house will be established at the summit of the mountains and raised above the hills,”
“and all the nations will stream to it.” And why does Isaiah say, “Listen, nations, to what I have done, and know my might, you who are far away”?
“The sinners in Zion were terrified, and trembling fell upon the godless.” What does this mean—that he makes known what he has done and reveals his might to those far away,
terrifies the sinners in Zion, and makes trembling fall upon the godless? For he calls the nations and through them provokes the people to jealousy, and he reveals his might to those far from him,
when he brings wrath to judge his people. He terrifies the sinners of Zion, which was called the holy city, and makes trembling fall upon the godless,
who are the false prophets, as he said about the prophets of Jerusalem: “From them godlessness has spread throughout the whole earth.”
You have heard, my dear friend, about this Passover of which I told you: its symbol was given to the former people, but its reality is proclaimed today among the nations.
For the minds of childish and uneducated people are very confused about this great festival day, asking how they are to recognize it and observe it.
For our Savior is the true lamb, a year old and without blemish, as the prophet said of him: “There is no wrongdoing in him,”
“nor was deceit found in his mouth. But the Lord desired that he be humbled and made to suffer.” As for calling him a year old,
this is because he was a child with regard to sins, as he said to his disciples, “Unless you turn and become like these children,”
“you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.” And Isaiah said about the righteous person, “The child who sins will die a hundred years old and be accursed.”
For our Savior ate the Passover with his disciples on the night of vigil, the fourteenth, and he enacted the sign of the Passover in its reality for his disciples.
After Judas had left them, he took bread, blessed it, gave it to his disciples, and said to them, “This is my body. Take and eat of it, all of you.”
Likewise, he also blessed the wine and said to them, “This is my blood of the new covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.”
“This is what you are to do in remembrance of me whenever you gather together,” he said, before our Lord was arrested.
After saying these things, our Lord rose from the place where he had celebrated the Passover and given his body to eat and his blood to drink.
He went with his disciples to the place where he was arrested. For from the time his body was eaten and his blood was drunk, he was counted among the dead.
With his own hands our Lord gave his body to eat, and before he was crucified he gave his blood to drink.
He was arrested on the night of the fourteenth and was tried until the sixth hour. At the sixth hour they condemned him, took him up, and crucified him.
For while they were trying him, he did not speak, and he gave no answer to his judges. He could have spoken and given an answer,
but it was not possible for someone counted among the dead to speak. From the sixth hour to the ninth there was darkness.
He entrusted his spirit to his Father at the ninth hour. He was among the dead on the night leading into the fifteenth—the night before the Sabbath—and throughout the whole day,
and for three hours on Friday. On the night leading into Sunday, at the time when he had given his body and blood to his disciples, he rose from among the dead.
Now show us, then, wise man, which are the three days and three nights that our Savior spent among the dead.
For we see three hours on Friday, the night leading into the Sabbath, and the whole day; and on Sunday night he rose.
Count them up for me: where are these three days and three nights? For look, they amounted to one complete day and night.
But truly, as our Savior said, “Just as Jonah son of Amittai was in the belly of the fish for three days and three nights,
so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth.” For the reckoning begins from the time when he gave his body to eat and his blood to drink.
In this way they amount to three days and three nights. For it says that it was nighttime when Judas went out from them,
and his eleven disciples ate our Savior’s body and drank his blood. So here is one night, the night leading into Friday.
And until the sixth hour, they tried him. So here are one day and one night. And the three hours when there was darkness, from the sixth hour to the ninth,
together with the three hours after the darkness—here are two days and two nights. And the complete night leading into the Sabbath, and the whole Sabbath day:
thus three days and three nights were completed for our Lord among the dead. And on Sunday night he rose from among the dead.
For the Jewish Passover is the fourteenth day, its night and its daytime. Ours, the day of the great suffering, is Friday,
the fifteenth day, its night and its daytime. Then, after the Passover, Israel ate unleavened bread for seven days, until the twenty-first of the month.
